# Project Viewpoint Addon API

> Write an addon, a resource pack or a Shaderpack for Viewpoint, and manage the packages you install.

- [Start here](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/start/introduction.md)
- [For players](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/players/managing-addons.md)
- [Getting started](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/start/getting-started.md)
- [The descriptor](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/descriptor.md)

For an AI agent: the list of every page is [llms.txt](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/llms.txt).

- [Start](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/start/introduction.md): What a package is. How to make the smallest addon. The samples.
- [For players](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/players/managing-addons.md): Install, order and switch packages. Read a label.
- [Concepts](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/package-kinds.md): The three kinds of package, the descriptor, the states, the versions and the order.
- [API 1.0](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/view-state.md): The view state, settings, services, the camera, the fight, models and shader values.
- [Patching](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/managed-patching.md): Declare hooks into game methods and into Viewpoint. Viewpoint installs, orders and lists them.
- [Labels & consent](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/trust/labels.md): Permissions, labels, consent and updates.
- [Performance](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/performance/assets-and-budgets.md): The memory pools, the estimates, and how to measure your package.
- [Resource packs](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/resource-packs/format.md): Models, tiles, sounds and data, with no code.
- [Shaderpacks](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/shaderpacks/format.md): Change how Viewpoint draws the world, with GLSL files and no Java.
- [Reference](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/reference/descriptor-keys.md): Descriptor keys, labels, permissions, the internals list and a glossary.

---

# Introduction

> What a Viewpoint package is, what it can do in API 1.0, and what Viewpoint does with it.

Viewpoint is a mod for Project Zomboid. It draws the game in first and third person. Other authors can add to it with
addons, resource packs and Shaderpacks. Players see each package and control it from the settings window.

## The three kinds of package

| Kind | Contains | Descriptor |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Addon** | Java code. It can also contain assets, shader snippets and Lua. | `addon.properties` |
| **Resource Pack** | Models, tiles, sounds and data. No Java and no shader code. | `pack.properties` |
| **Shaderpack** | GLSL files and their options. No Java. | `pack.properties` |

A model pack in the older Viewpoint model pack format is a resource pack with the *legacy* flag. See
[Package kinds](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/package-kinds.md).

## What Viewpoint does with your package

- It loads your jar in a class loader of its own. Your code can use `viewpoint.api`, and the members of Viewpoint that
  are on the [internals list](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/reference/viewpoint-internals.md).
- It shows your package in the settings window: an addon in **Advanced**, **Addons**, a resource pack in **Graphics**,
  **Resource Packs**, and a Shaderpack in **Graphics**, **Shaderpacks**. The player orders it, switches it on and off, and reads what it does. A
  restart is not necessary.
- It checks your jar when it loads it, and shows a label: **Normal**, **Amber** or **Red**. See [Labels](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/trust/labels.md).
- It installs the hooks that you declare, runs them in the player's order, and lists each active hook.
- It gives you files, downloads and assets through its services. Each service has a permission and limits.

## What you can do in API 1.0

| To do this | Use | Page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read where the view is and what it shows | `ViewState`, `ViewListener` | [View state](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/view-state.md) |
| Give settings and key bindings | `settings.properties`, `AddonSettings`, `KeyAction` | [Settings & keys](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/settings-and-keys.md) |
| Read the view state from Lua | `Viewpoint.Addons` | [Lua mirror](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/lua-mirror.md) |
| Give your Java functions to Lua | `@LuaExport` | [Lua exports](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/lua-exports.md) |
| Keep files | `AddonFiles` | [Files](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/files.md) |
| Get a file from the internet | `AddonDownloads` | [Downloads](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/downloads.md) |
| Load models, textures, sounds and data | `AddonAssets` | [Assets](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/assets.md) |
| Give a feature to other addons | `Services` | [Services](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/services.md) |
| Move the camera | `CameraLayer`, `CameraClaim` | [Camera layers](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/camera-layers.md) |
| Follow the aim and the shots | `AimListener`, `ShotListener` | [Aim & shots](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/aim-and-shots.md) |
| Choose the model of an object | `ModelProvider`, `AttachmentProvider` | [Model providers](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/model-providers.md) |
| Give numbers to shader code | `ShaderValues` | [Shader values](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/shader-values.md) |
| Add a piece of GLSL to a shader | `AddonSnippets` | [Shader snippets](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/shader-snippets.md) |
| Draw with OpenGL | `DrawCallback`, `Gpu` | [Draw callbacks](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/draw-callbacks.md) (planned) |
| Change what a game method does | `@Hook` | [Managed patching](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/managed-patching.md) |
| Change what a method of Viewpoint does | `@Hook` on a listed member | [Hooking Viewpoint](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/hooking-viewpoint.md) |
| Replace the game's tile art | The `tiles` folder of a resource pack | [Tiles](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/resource-packs/tiles.md) |
| Choose a model from the state of an object | A version 2 manifest | [Model states](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/resource-packs/model-states.md) |
| Change how the whole frame looks | A Shaderpack | [Shaderpack format](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/shaderpacks/format.md) |

A page marked *planned* is not written yet. Its feature is part of API 1.0. The sidebar group **Planned** lists these pages.

> **ZombieBuddy mods are different**
>
> A mod that loads its Java through ZombieBuddy (`javaJarFile` in `mod.info`) is not managed by Viewpoint. Viewpoint
> shows it as **Unmanaged**. Viewpoint cannot order it, switch it off or check it. To change such a mod into an addon,
> read [Migrating from ZombieBuddy](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/migrating-from-zombiebuddy.md).

licence. The font of these pages is Roboto Medium, under the Apache 2.0 licence ([notice](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/notices/Roboto.txt)).

5. [Glossary](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/reference/glossary.md): the terms these pages use.

# Getting started

> Make the smallest addon, put it in a mod and switch it on.

This page makes an addon that writes a line to the game's log when it switches on and off. The addon has three
parts: a descriptor, a jar with one class, and a mod folder. The code on this page is the code of
`minimaladdon` in the source repository. [`sampleaddon`](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/start/sample-walkthrough.md) has a part for each service.

## What you need

- Viewpoint, in the game's mod list.
- `viewpoint-api.jar`. Each Viewpoint release has this jar, with its sources and javadoc. It contains only
  `viewpoint.api.*`. Compile against it. Do not put it in your mod.
- A JDK and a build tool. The example uses Gradle.

> **Note**
>
> Compile for Java 17 (`--release 17`). Viewpoint refuses a jar that contains its own copy of `viewpoint.api`.

## The folder

An addon is in a Project Zomboid mod. Viewpoint looks for it in the mod's version folder first, then in `common/`.

- ViewpointMinimalAddon/
  - common/
    - mod.info
    - media/viewpoint/addons/example.minimal/
      - addon.properties
      - minimal.jar
      - icon.png optional
      - settings.properties optional
      - CHANGELOG.md optional

The name of the folder under `addons/` must be the same as the addon's `id`.

`mod.info` is the usual file of the game. Put it in `common/` or in the version folder: the game does not read one at the
root of the mod. Require Viewpoint. **Do not set `javaJarFile`.** If you set it, ZombieBuddy
loads the jar, and Viewpoint shows the mod as Unmanaged. Name the jar with `jar=` in `addon.properties`.

```properties title="mod.info"
name=Viewpoint Minimal Addon
id=ViewpointMinimalAddon
require=Viewpoint
description=The smallest addon of Viewpoint's guide.
```

## The descriptor

```properties title="addon.properties"
format=1
id=example.minimal
name=Minimal
version=0.1.0
author=Viewpoint
description=Writes a line to the log when it switches on and off.
license=MIT
game.min=42.21
api=1.0
jar=minimal.jar
entry=example.minimal.MinimalAddon
side=client
```

An addon must have `game.min`, `api`, `jar` and `entry`. The [Descriptor](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/descriptor.md) page gives all keys.
This addon asks for no permission, because it uses no service that needs one.

## The class

```java title="MinimalAddon.java"
package example.minimal;

import viewpoint.api.Addon;
import viewpoint.api.AddonContext;

/** The smallest addon: it writes a line to the log when it starts, when its hooks are live and when it stops. */
public final class MinimalAddon implements Addon {
    @Override
    public void enable(AddonContext ctx) {
        System.out.println("[Minimal] " + ctx.id() + " is on");
        ctx.onHooksLive(() -> System.out.println("[Minimal] hooks are live"));
    }

    @Override
    public void disable() {
        System.out.println("[Minimal] off");
    }
}
```

`enable` runs on the game's main thread when the player switches the addon on. The callback that you give to
`onHooksLive` also runs on the main thread. This addon has no hooks, so Viewpoint calls it at once. A `disable` method is
not necessary. When the player switches the addon off, Viewpoint closes each `Registration` that it gave you, in
reverse order. Keep a `Registration` only to close it before that.

## The build

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
plugins {
    java
}

java {
    toolchain.languageVersion = JavaLanguageVersion.of(25)
}

tasks.withType<JavaCompile> {
    options.release = 17
}

dependencies {
    compileOnly(files("libs/viewpoint-api.jar"))
}

tasks.jar {
    archiveFileName = "minimal.jar"
}
```

`compileOnly` keeps the API out of your jar. Copy `build/libs/minimal.jar` into the folder of `addon.properties`.

## Switch it on

1. In the game's mod list, enable `ViewpointMinimalAddon` and `Viewpoint`.
2. Start the game. Viewpoint reads the mod list only when the game starts.
3. Open the settings window. Go to **Advanced**, **Addons**.
4. Find the **Minimal** card in the **Inactive** column. A new addon always starts there.
5. Put the pointer on the card and click the green tick, or double-click the card.
6. Read the label and the consent dialog. Click to accept.
7. Make sure that the card is in the **Active** column.
8. Look in the game's `console.txt`. It shows `[Minimal] example.minimal is on` and `[Minimal] hooks are live`.
9. Click the red minus on the card. The file shows `[Minimal] off`.

After you switch it off, none of the code of the addon runs. If you change the jar, the next enable loads the new
jar. If the new jar asks for more, the player must give consent again. See
[Lifecycle & threads](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/lifecycle-and-threads.md) and [Updates & changelogs](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/trust/updates-and-changelogs.md).

## Next

- Add a [setting and a key](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/settings-and-keys.md).
- Read the [view state](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/view-state.md) of every frame.
- Hook a game method with [managed patching](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/managed-patching.md).
- Add an [offset to the camera](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/camera-layers.md) with a layer.
- Make a [Shaderpack](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/shaderpacks/format.md) or a [resource pack](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/resource-packs/format.md) in place of an addon, if you
  have no code. See [Package kinds](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/package-kinds.md).

## If it does not appear

| You see | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No card | The mod was off when the game started, or the folder name is not the `id`. | Enable the mod and start the game again. Make the folder name the same as the `id`. |
| **Incompatible** | `game.min`, `game.max`, `viewpoint.min`, `viewpoint.max` or `api` does not agree with this installation. | Read the card. It names the range. Correct the range or the build. |
| **Failed** | The jar did not load, or `entry` is not a class that implements `Addon`. | Read the card and `console.txt`. They give the cause. |
| Nothing occurs when you click the green tick | The check refused the jar, or the ZombieBuddy policy blocks addons with Java. | Read the card. It gives the cause. See [ZombieBuddy policy & signatures](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/trust/relation-to-zombiebuddy.md). |

---

# Sample walkthrough

> The sample addon, the sample resource pack and the sample Shaderpack, and what each part shows.

Viewpoint's source repository has three samples and one legacy model pack. The code on these pages comes from the
samples.

## Use the samples

1. Build the samples. Run `gradlew samples` in the source repository. It makes a mod folder for each sample, for example
   `sampleaddon/build/mod/ViewpointSampleAddon`.
2. Copy their mod folders into the game's mods folder.
3. Enable the sample mods and Viewpoint in the game's mod list.
4. Start the game.
5. Open **Advanced**, **Addons** for the sample addon, and **Graphics**, **Resource Packs** for the sample resource pack. The samples are in the **Inactive** column, as all new packages are. The sample Shaderpack is in **Graphics**, **Shaderpacks**.
6. Switch them on.

## `sampleaddon`

One addon. It has one small part for each service of the API. Each part is one small class.

- sampleaddon/
  - build.gradle.kts
  - addon.properties
  - settings.properties
  - mod.info
  - CHANGELOG.md
  - models/
  - sounds/
  - data/
  - src/main/java/example/sample/
    - SampleAddon.java
    - ViewPart.java
    - and one file for each other part

The classes of an addon cannot be in a package that starts with `viewpoint.`, because Viewpoint reserves it. The sample
uses `example.sample`. It has these parts:

| Part | What it does | Page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SampleAddon` | Starts the parts. Writes a line to the log when the addon switches on, when its hooks are live, and when it switches off. | [Getting started](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/start/getting-started.md) |
| `ViewPart` | A `ViewListener`. Once a second, it writes the eye's height and the ground height under the crosshair. | [View state](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/view-state.md) |
| `SettingsPart` | One toggle, two numbers and one key. The key writes a line when you push it. It also adds a settings page, with a button and two value rows. | [Settings & keys](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/settings-and-keys.md) |
| `FilesPart` | Writes a counter with `AddonFiles` at each enable, and reads it again. | [Files](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/files.md) |
| `DownloadPart` | Asks to download one small file when you click its button on the settings page. The player sees the prompt each time. | [Downloads](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/downloads.md) |
| `HookPart` | One `@Hook.Before` hook on a game method. Its handler only reads the call. | [Managed patching](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/managed-patching.md) |
| `ViewpointHookPart` | One hook on a listed method of Viewpoint. The render thread calls that method, so the hook has `thread = ANY`, with a typed handler. | [Hooking Viewpoint](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/hooking-viewpoint.md) |
| `ExportPart` | Gives one Java function to Lua: `Sample.twice(21)`. | [Lua exports](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/lua-exports.md) |
| `CameraPart` | A camera layer that rolls the view a little while the key is down. | [Camera layers](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/camera-layers.md) |
| `ShotPart` | A `ShotListener` that writes the number of hits of each shot. | [Aim & shots](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/aim-and-shots.md) |
| `DrawPart` | A draw callback that draws one small triangle with `Gpu`, in the top right corner of the screen. | [Draw callbacks](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/draw-callbacks.md) |
| `SnippetPart` | A shader snippet that tints the light at `colour.end`. While it links, the game pauses. | [Shader snippets](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/shader-snippets.md) |
| `ValuesPart` | Sets a shader value that the snippet reads. | [Shader values](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/shader-values.md) |
| `AssetsPart` | Writes what its model and its texture take, reads one data file, and loads and plays one sound. | [Assets](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/assets.md) |

The descriptor asks only for the permissions that the sample uses. See [Permissions](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/trust/permissions.md).

The card shows the label of the sample. Open the card's **Info**. Read **Trust**, then **Permissions**, then **Hooks**.
The player reads these tabs before they give consent. Look at them once from the player's side.

## `sampleresourcepack`

A resource pack, with no code.

- sampleresourcepack/
  - pack.properties
  - mod.info
  - CHANGELOG.md
  - models/
  - tiles/
  - sounds/

It has these parts:

- a version 2 manifest with a model on one sprite, a lamp whose shade changes when it is lit, and a chair bound for all its
  facings by one line;
- a floor and a wall, each with its normal and specular texture;
- one sound, which the card includes. Viewpoint does not play the sounds of a resource pack.

See [Format](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/resource-packs/format.md), [Model states](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/resource-packs/model-states.md) and
[Tiles](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/resource-packs/tiles.md).

## `sampleshaderpack`

A Shaderpack, with no Java.

- sampleshaderpack/
  - pack.properties
  - mod.info
  - CHANGELOG.md
  - shaders/
    - tint.frag

It builds on the `default` pack. It adds one option and one pass at the `final` stage. See
[Shaderpack format](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/shaderpacks/format.md) and [Passes & inputs](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/shaderpacks/passes-and-inputs.md).

## The legacy model pack

`samplelegacypack` is a small mod. Its Lua calls `Viewpoint.ModelPacks.register`, as older model packs do. Viewpoint shows
it as the resource pack `legacy.ViewpointSampleLegacyPack`, with the *legacy* flag. Its manifest is version 1. It shows that older packs continue to work and follow the player's order. Do not copy it for a new pack.
See [Legacy model packs](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/resource-packs/legacy-model-packs.md).

## Try these changes

1. Increase the sample's `version`. Build it again. The card shows a dot. Click **Info** and open the **Changelog** tab.
2. Change the line to `downloads.hosts=example.com,example.org`. The addon now asks for more. It stays off until you give
   consent again.
3. In **Info**, **Hooks**, veto the hook. At the next safe point, the game runs as if the addon has no hook.
4. Drag the sample above or below a different addon. The order in the hook list changes.
5. In **Graphics**, **Shaderpacks**, click the green tick on `sampleshaderpack`. Change its option in **Graphics**, **Shader Options**.

---

# Package kinds

> The three kinds of package, the legacy and Unmanaged flags, and which kind to make.

Viewpoint has three kinds of package. Each package that Viewpoint shows, orders and switches is one of them.

| | Addon | Resource Pack | Shaderpack |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Contains | Java in a jar, assets, shader snippets, Lua | Assets only: `models/`, `tiles/`, `sounds/`, `data/` | GLSL files, their options, and `textures/` |
| Descriptor | `media/viewpoint/addons/<id>/addon.properties` | `media/viewpoint/resourcepacks/<id>/pack.properties` | `media/viewpoint/shaderpacks/<id>/pack.properties` |
| Java | A jar, named by `jar=`. Never by `javaJarFile`. | None | None |
| Shader code | Snippets and `Gpu` programs, with permissions | None | GLSL files of the pack |
| Permissions | In the descriptor | None | None |
| The label tells about | The Java, the assets, the Lua line and the shader line | The assets and the Lua line | The GLSL, the Lua line and the shader line |

Make a resource pack if you have only files: a model for a sprite, a set of tiles. Make a
Shaderpack if you change how Viewpoint draws the whole frame. Make an addon if you need code, or to play a sound or read a data file. An addon can also contain
assets, with the same four keys as a resource pack.

## Where each one goes

Viewpoint looks in the mod's version folder first, then in `common/`.

If the same folder name is in both, Viewpoint uses the package in the version folder.

- MyMod/
  - mod.info
  - 42/
    - media/viewpoint/addons/example.lean/
      - addon.properties
  - common/
    - media/viewpoint/resourcepacks/example.tiles/
      - pack.properties
    - media/viewpoint/shaderpacks/example.dusk/
      - pack.properties
      - shaders/

One mod can contain many packages. Each package has its own id. The folder name must be the same as the id.

## Packs that are not packages

Two older kinds of shader pack continue to work. They are not packages.

- **Folder packs.** A pack in the folder `Zomboid/viewpoint-shaderpacks/<name>/`. The player puts it there. It has no
  consent and no descriptor of the package kind.
- **Iris packs.** A shader pack made for Minecraft, as a `.zip` or a folder in the same folder. Viewpoint reads it in place.

The **Graphics**, **Shaderpacks** page lists them beside the packages. See [Shaderpacks for players](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/players/shaderpacks.md).

## Legacy and Unmanaged are flags

**Legacy.** A model pack in the older Viewpoint model pack format has no descriptor. The mod's Lua registers a manifest:

```lua
Viewpoint.ModelPacks.register("MyPackMod", "media/models/pack.json")
```

Viewpoint shows this pack as a resource pack with the id `legacy.<modId>` and the *legacy* flag. The version and the
game range come from `mod.info`. A legacy pack follows the player's order and switch, as all packages do. See
[Legacy model packs](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/resource-packs/legacy-model-packs.md).

**Unmanaged.** A mod that has `javaJarFile` in `mod.info` and requires Viewpoint is loaded by ZombieBuddy. Viewpoint
does not load it. Viewpoint shows it on a card, with a label that comes from `mod.info` only:

- Amber: **Unmanaged: runs outside Viewpoint's controls (hooks cannot be listed, ordered or vetoed)**
- Red, when the mod starts before Viewpoint: **loads before Viewpoint**

Viewpoint does not read the jar of an Unmanaged mod. Viewpoint cannot order it, switch it off, or show what it does. To
change it into an addon, see [Migrating from ZombieBuddy](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/migrating-from-zombiebuddy.md).

> **Note**
>
> The Unmanaged flag comes from how the mod loads, not from its code. Put the same code in an addon, and Viewpoint checks,
> orders and switches it.

## What the player sees

Each kind has a page of its own in the settings window: **Advanced**, **Addons**; **Graphics**, **Resource Packs**; and
**Graphics**, **Shaderpacks**. The first two have an **Inactive** column and an **Active** column. When two packages change the same thing, the package nearer the top of the
Active column wins. The Shaderpacks page has no order. See [Order](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/order.md) and
[Managing addons](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/players/managing-addons.md).

## Ids

Make an id from lower-case letters and digits. You can put `-` and `.` between them.

- Use 2 to 64 characters.
- Start and end the id with a letter or a digit.
- Do not put two dots together.
- Do not start the id with the name of a Windows device (`con`, `nul`, `com1` and others), also before a dot.
- Do not start the id with `legacy.` or `legacy-`. Viewpoint uses this start for the older model packs that it finds in
  mods.

Examples: `example.lean`, `my-tiles`.

Start your id with your reversed domain or your name, as `example.lean` does. Then two authors do not use the same id.
Viewpoint refuses a second package whose id differs from an installed id only in the case of the letters.

### The encoded id

Settings keys and GLSL names cannot hold `.` or `-`. In these places Viewpoint writes both as `_`:

| For the id `example.lean` | You see |
| --- | --- |
| A setting of an addon | `addon.example_lean.angle` |
| An option of a Shaderpack | `pack.example_lean.warmth` |
| A shader value of an addon | `uAddon_example_lean_angle` |

Viewpoint refuses a package when its encoded id is the same as the encoded id of an installed package. For example,
`my-tiles` and `my.tiles` cannot be installed together.

If Viewpoint does not accept an id, the card tells you. Use a short lower-case id, with your name as the first part.

---

# Descriptor

> All keys of addon.properties and pack.properties, and what Viewpoint does with each key.

The descriptor is one text file: `addon.properties` for an addon, `pack.properties` for a resource pack or a Shaderpack.
It is a Java properties file in UTF-8. A comment is a full line that starts with `#`. A `#` after a value is part of the
value.

The folder of the file tells Viewpoint the kind: `addons/`, `resourcepacks/` or `shaderpacks/`. See
[Package kinds](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/package-kinds.md).

```properties title="addon.properties"
format=1
id=example.lean
name=Lean
version=1.2.0
author=Example
description=Lean round corners.
icon=icon.png
license=MIT
game.min=42.21
game.max=42.21
viewpoint.min=0.1.7
viewpoint.max=0.2.99
api=1.0
jar=lean.jar
entry=com.example.lean.LeanAddon
side=client
requires=example.core@1.0
conflicts=other.lean
settings=settings.properties
changelog=CHANGELOG.md
permissions=hooks,files,downloads,lua,camera
hooks.targets=zombie.characters.IsoPlayer
files.quotaMiB=16
downloads.hosts=github.com,objects.githubusercontent.com
lua.globals=Lean
exports=com.example.lean.api
```

Viewpoint ignores a key that it does not know, and writes it to the log. If `format` is newer than the format that
Viewpoint reads, the package is **Incompatible**. The card tells you this.

Viewpoint **refuses** a package when a required key is missing or a value is not valid. For example: an id that does not
follow the [rules for ids](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/package-kinds.md#ids), a version that is not dotted numbers, a path that goes out of
the package folder (with `..`), or a permission that Viewpoint does not know. The card names each key and tells why. The
player cannot switch on a refused package. Viewpoint also refuses a descriptor that is larger than 64 KiB.

## Common keys

All descriptors use these keys.

| Key | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `format` | Yes | The format of the descriptor: `1`. |
| `id` | Yes | The id of the package (see [Ids](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/package-kinds.md#ids)). The folder name must be the same. |
| `name` | Yes | The name on the card. |
| `version` | Yes | The version of the package: major, minor and patch, each of at most three digits (`MMM.NNN.PPP`, for example `1.2.0`). Consent is for one version. |
| `author` | No | The name of the author on the card. |
| `description` | No | One or two lines on the card. |
| `icon` | No | A PNG file in the package folder. If there is no icon, the card shows a tile with a letter. |
| `license` | No | The name of the licence, on the **Overview** tab. A Shaderpack card shows it also on the label. |
| `game.min` | Yes | The oldest game build that can run the package, for example `42.21`. |
| `game.max` | No | The newest game build. If you do not set it, all newer builds are accepted. |
| `viewpoint.min`, `viewpoint.max` | No | The range of Viewpoint versions. |
| `requires` | No | Packages that must be active, as `id` or `id@min`, with commas between them. |
| `conflicts` | No | Packages that must not be active at the same time, as ids with commas between them. |
| `changelog` | No | A file of `## <version>` sections, shown as plain text. |

## Addon keys

Only `addon.properties` uses these keys. Another descriptor ignores them.

| Key | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `side` | No | `client` (the default) or `gameplay`. See [`side`](#side). |
| `api` | Yes | The API version that you compiled against: `1.0`. See [Versions & compatibility](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/versions-and-compatibility.md). |
| `jar` | Yes | The name of the jar in the package folder. Do not use `javaJarFile`. |
| `entry` | Yes | The class that implements `Addon`. |
| `settings` | No | A `settings.properties` file. See [Settings & keys](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/settings-and-keys.md). |
| `permissions` | No | A list of the permissions that the addon asks for, with commas between them. See [Permissions](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/trust/permissions.md). |
| `hooks.targets` | With `hooks` | The classes that the addon can hook, with commas between them. A game class or a listed class of Viewpoint. See [Hookable targets](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/hookable-targets.md). |
| `files.quotaMiB` | No | The space for the files folder of the addon, in MiB. The default is 64. More than 64 needs the player's consent. |
| `draw.gpuMiB` | No | The video memory for the `Gpu` objects of the addon, in MiB, 1 or more. The default is 64. More than 128 needs the permission `vram`. See [Draw callbacks](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/draw-callbacks.md). |
| `downloads.hosts` | With `downloads` | The hosts that the addon can download from, with commas between them. |
| `lua.globals` | No | Names of Lua globals for your exports, with commas between them. Without it, the exports are in `Viewpoint.Addons["<id>"]`. |
| `exports` | No | The Java packages that other addons can link to. See [Services](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/services.md). |

## Asset keys

An addon and a resource pack use these keys. A Shaderpack does not.

| Key | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `models`, `tiles`, `sounds`, `data` | No | The assets. `models` is the path of a model manifest. The other three are folders. See [Format](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/resource-packs/format.md). |

## Shaderpack keys

A Shaderpack uses the common keys, and the keys of its pack. It has no `jar`, `entry`, `api` or `permissions`. It can
also set `library`, the Viewpoint version that you made the pack for. See [Shaderpack format](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/shaderpacks/format.md).

## Version ranges

A version is dotted numbers, for example `42.21` or `0.1.7`. Viewpoint compares the numbers one by one. A missing number
is 0.

- `game.min` and `game.max` are game builds. A game build has two numbers, as `42.21`. `viewpoint.min` and
  `viewpoint.max` are Viewpoint versions. The range includes both limits.
- `requires=example.core@1.0` means `example.core`, version 1.0 or later, with the same major version.
- `api=1.0` means the same major version, and a minor version of 1.0 or more in Viewpoint.

A package outside its ranges is **Incompatible**. Its card names the range.

## `side`

Viewpoint runs only on the client. Your code runs on the client also when the server does not list your mod.

| Value | Use it when the addon | What occurs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `client` | Changes only what the player sees or hears | The addon runs in single player and on all servers. |
| `gameplay` | Changes something that the server must also agree with | The addon runs in single player. On a server that does not list the addon's mod, Viewpoint suspends the addon for that session. |

## Permissions and their keys

`permissions` lists the services that the addon will ask Viewpoint for. Some permissions have keys of their own:

| Permission | Keys |
| --- | --- |
| `hooks` | `hooks.targets` |
| `files` | `files.quotaMiB` (optional) |
| `downloads` | `downloads.hosts` |
| `lua` | `lua.globals` (optional) |
| `draw` | `draw.gpuMiB` (optional) |
| `vram` | `draw.gpuMiB` more than 128 |
| `camera`, `combat`, `models`, `shaders` | None |

If you call a service without its permission, your code gets a `SecurityException`. If a hook target is not in
`hooks.targets`, the addon cannot start. The card tells you this before the player sees a consent dialog. See
[Permissions](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/trust/permissions.md).

## Encoded keys

A setting of an addon is saved as `addon.<encoded id>.<name>`. An option of a Shaderpack is saved as
`pack.<encoded id>.<option>`. A shader value is `uAddon_<encoded id>_<name>`. The encoded id writes `.` and `-` as `_`.
See [Package kinds](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/package-kinds.md#the-encoded-id).

## The descriptor of a resource pack

```properties title="pack.properties"
format=1
id=example.tiles
name=Example tiles
version=1.0.0
author=Example
game.min=42.21
tiles=tiles
sounds=sounds
```

It uses the common keys and the asset keys. It has no `jar`, `entry`, `api` or `permissions`, because it has no code.

> **Tip**
>
> The [Descriptor keys](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/reference/descriptor-keys.md) page has all keys in one table.

---

# Lifecycle & threads

> The states of a package, what runs when, and on which thread.

## The states

Each package has one state at a time. The card shows it. Viewpoint compares a package with this installation when it finds it.

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Incompatible** | Its game, Viewpoint or API range does not agree with this installation. You cannot switch it on. The card names the range. For a Shaderpack: **Incompatible: requires its base**. |
| **Refused** | Its descriptor or its files are wrong, or its `requires` make a cycle. You cannot switch it on. The card gives the cause. |
| **Inactive** | It can run, and it is off. A new package starts in this state. If something stops it, for example a package that it requires is off, the card says what. |
| **Waiting for \<package\>** | A Shaderpack that builds on another package that is not active. It starts when the other package is active. |
| **Checking** | Viewpoint reads the jar and checks its signature in the background. The package goes on when this is done: it asks for consent, or starts if the consent covers it. |
| **Awaiting consent** | The player clicked the green tick. Viewpoint checked the package and shows the consent dialog. |
| **Activating** | Viewpoint prepares the entry class and runs `enable`. |
| **Active** | Running. |
| **Active: hooks pending** | Running. Its hooks wait for the next safe point. |
| **Deactivating** | `disable` runs, and Viewpoint closes the registrations. |
| **Lingering** | Off, but Java has not yet released its classes from memory. The card shows **Inactive**. |
| **Failed** | It did not load, `enable` failed, or its hooks did not install. The card gives the cause. |
| **Suspended** | Stopped for this session. A handler threw an exception, or the server does not list the mod of a `side=gameplay` addon. |
| **Needs an update** | The addon uses a member of Viewpoint that Viewpoint has removed. The card names the member and the replacement, or says that nothing replaces it. See [Hooking Viewpoint](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/hooking-viewpoint.md#removed-members). |

A resource pack and a Shaderpack use the same states, but not the states that are about code.

## When Viewpoint finds packages

Viewpoint reads the game's mod list once, when the game starts. This list stays the same for the session. Addons
stay loaded when the player joins a server.

Viewpoint looks for packages at these times:

- when the game starts;
- when the player opens the **Addons** page or the **Resource Packs** page;
- when the player clicks **Rescan**.

A package that Viewpoint finds for the first time is always **Inactive**.

## The start of the game

If an enabled addon has the `lua` permission and gives functions to Lua, Viewpoint must start it before the Lua of the
mods runs. At the start of the game, Viewpoint checks and starts these addons, and it waits for them. The wait has a
short limit (about 5 seconds) in all. The screen shows the message "Viewpoint is checking N addons" during the wait.

- An addon that is ready before the limit has its Lua functions when the Lua of the mods starts.
- An addon that is not ready at the limit starts at the first frame. Its Lua functions come late. The card says "its Lua
  functions came late at this start".
- Viewpoint checks the addons that give functions to Lua first.
- When a world loads, or when the player returns to the menu, the functions install again, with no wait.

Keep your addon small and fast to load. A jar that is large or slow can miss the limit.

## Enabling

When the player switches an addon on, Viewpoint does these steps on the main thread:

1. It reads and checks the jar.
2. It compares the addon with the player's consent. If the addon asks for more than before, the player must give
   consent again.
3. It loads the classes from the bytes of the jar that it checked, in a class loader of the addon's own. It starts
   an addon only from a jar that is the same as the one that it checked. If the file on disk changed after the check
   and Viewpoint no longer has the bytes that it checked, the addon does not start: the card shows **Failed**, and
   Viewpoint checks the jar again when the player switches the addon on. No other addon shares a class with it.
4. It prepares the entry class and the class of each handler. If a static initialiser throws an exception, the enable
   fails.
5. It runs `enable(AddonContext)`. Each listener or callback that you register through the context gives you a `Registration`.
6. It puts your hooks in a queue for the next safe point.

If a step fails, Viewpoint closes your registrations in reverse order. The addon goes to **Failed** or **Inactive**. The
game does not change.

### Safe points

Viewpoint installs and removes hooks only at safe points, on the main thread:

- in the main menu;
- while a world loads;
- in a paused single-player game, with the game window open.

On a server, only the main menu and the loading screen are safe points. The card then shows *applies at the main menu*.
Between the switch-on and the next safe point, the state is **Active: hooks pending**.

To know when your hooks are installed, use one of these:

- `ctx.hooksLive()` tells you if they are installed now.
- `ctx.onHooksLive(Runnable)` calls your code when they are installed.

## Disabling

When the player switches the addon off:

1. Viewpoint runs your `disable()`, if you wrote one.
2. Viewpoint closes each `Registration` in reverse order. It does this also if `disable` throws an exception.
3. Viewpoint frees the buffers, textures and programs that you made with `Gpu`.
4. Viewpoint removes your hooks at the next safe point.

`disable` is optional. If you get all your resources as a `Registration`, you do not have to write it.

If another addon has your addon in `requires`, Viewpoint first asks to switch that addon off. When a Shaderpack builds on
your package, it waits for the package to come back.

The addon is **Lingering** until Java releases your classes from memory. Its card shows it as **Inactive**. If Java still
holds them one minute after the addon closed, Viewpoint writes a line with the id of the addon to `console.txt`. In
`disable`, remove everything of your addon from places outside it, for example from lists of the game. If something still
refers to your classes, the addon stays **Lingering** until the game restarts, and `console.txt` has that line.

Three things keep your classes in memory that Viewpoint cannot clear for you. Do these in `disable`:

- **Stop your threads.** A thread that you start inside `enable` gets your addon as its context loader and holds it
  until the thread ends.
- **Clear your `ThreadLocal` values** on each thread that set one. A value of your class holds your classes.
- **Do not keep your objects outside your addon.** This includes a `ClassValue`, a listener that you gave to the game, and
  a list of another addon.

## Updates

A loaded addon keeps the jar that it loaded, in memory. If the files on disk change, also if only the jar changes, the
card shows a dot and *update available, applies at next enable or restart*. The next enable reads the new jar and compares it with the player's consent. An
update that asks for more never starts without the player's consent. This is also true after a restart. See
[Updates & changelogs](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/trust/updates-and-changelogs.md).

## Suspension

If a `Throwable` goes out of one of your handlers or callbacks, Viewpoint suspends the addon for the session. Viewpoint
writes this line and the stack trace to `console.txt`:

```text
[Viewpoint] addon example.lean suspended: <hook> threw ...
```

To try again, the player switches the addon on again.

The server's list of mods applies from the end of the connection's handshake, when the game has joined the server. Before
that, and after a join that failed, Viewpoint uses no list. When the server does not list the mod of a `side=gameplay`
addon, Viewpoint suspends the addon, and also each package that requires it. They start again when the player leaves the server or joins one that lists the mod, if the rules and the
player's consent still allow it. An addon that a handler suspended stays off for the whole session.

When Viewpoint suspends an addon, it releases each claim that the addon holds (camera, view, cursor, shot resolver and
reticle). The release happens at the start of the next frame. The frame that is being drawn keeps its values.

## Threads

Almost all of your code runs on the game's **main thread**:

- `enable` and `disable`;
- hook handlers (except `thread = ANY` and `thread = RENDER`, see below);
- view listeners, aim and shot listeners, camera layers and claims, and providers;
- services, and the calls of Lua to your exports;
- setting and key callbacks;
- the callbacks of a `Pending`;
- `ShaderValues.set`.

Viewpoint does file work, downloads and asset decoding on its own threads. You get each result on the main thread.

### The render thread

Your code runs on the render thread only in two places:

- a **draw callback**, which uses the `Gpu` object and a short list of OpenGL calls. See
  [Draw callbacks](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/draw-callbacks.md) (planned);
- a hook with `thread = RENDER`, which can read and set values only. It cannot draw.

Viewpoint measures each of these calls. If one throws an exception, Viewpoint suspends the addon. Values from the main
thread, such as shader values and view poses, reach the render thread in a copy of the frame. You do not read game
objects on the render thread.

The javadoc of each public API method has a `@thread` tag. It tells you the thread that can call the method.

> **A handler that does not return stops the game**
>
> Your handlers run on the main thread, or on the render thread. If a handler loops forever, the game stops. Viewpoint
> cannot stop the handler.

### Hooks and other threads

A hook has `thread = MAIN` by default. If the game calls the hooked method from a different thread, Viewpoint **does
not run your handler**. The card counts the call as *skipped off-thread*. You can use `thread = ANY` for a handler that
reads only values. See [Managed patching](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/managed-patching.md#threads).

## Re-entry

While your handler runs, Viewpoint does not run your handlers again. If your handler calls a hooked method, the call
does not recurse into your handlers. The card counts these skipped calls.

---

# Versions & compatibility

> The versions of the API, what stays the same in 1.x, what occurs when Viewpoint removes an internal member, and what occurs when a build does not agree.

## The API version

`viewpoint-api.jar` contains only `viewpoint.api.**`. It has its own version, with semantic versioning. This version is
not the same as the Viewpoint version.

- **In 1.x,** changes only add. New types and new methods come with a `default` body. An interface that addons
  implement never gets a new abstract method.
- **Deprecated members** stay for two releases. Then they are removed.
- **Use `viewpoint.api` when you can.** You can also use or hook some of Viewpoint's internal members. They are in the
  [Viewpoint internals list](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/reference/viewpoint-internals.md). Internal members can change in each release, and they
  give your addon an Amber or Red label. Viewpoint does not load a jar that uses an internal member that is not in the
  list.

At run time, Viewpoint uses only its own copy of the API. Viewpoint refuses a jar that contains `viewpoint.api` classes.

## Tell Viewpoint the API version

Set `api=1.0` in the descriptor to the version that you compiled against. Viewpoint accepts the addon if the major
version is the same and its own minor version is the same or higher.

## Ask what is available

`Version.API` is the API version of the installed Viewpoint. To use a feature that comes after 1.0, and also run on
1.0, ask for the feature first:

```java
if (Version.has("view.pose", 2)) {
    // the second generation of the pose is available
}
```

`has(capability, generation)` tells you if a generation of a capability is available. The javadoc of the type that adds
a capability gives its name and generations.

The passes of a Shaderpack have a version also. Ask for it with `Version.has("passes", generation)`.

## Internal members change

The members of Viewpoint on the internals list have no promise of stability. Each release can add, deprecate or remove
members. [Internals changes](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/reference/internals-changes.md) lists the changes of each release.

| The member is | What occurs |
| --- | --- |
| **Deprecated** | The addon works. The card shows the replacement and the Amber reason **uses deprecated internals**. |
| **Removed** | The addon shows **Needs an update: uses \<member\>, removed in \<release\>; use \<replacement\>**. It does not start. |

A removed member stays in the list as a record, so that the card can tell the author what to use. Test your addon with
each release that your players use.

## The game and Viewpoint

Set `game.min`, `game.max`, `viewpoint.min` and `viewpoint.max` to the builds that you tested. Outside this range the
package is **Incompatible**, and the player cannot switch it on. The card names the limit.

Viewpoint supports one game build. On a different game build, Viewpoint stays off, and all addons stay off with it.
Your ranges do not change this.

## Errors

| You see | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Failed: built for another API** | Your code needs a class or method that this API does not have. Java throws a `LinkageError` during `enable`. | Compile against the API version that you set in `api`. Use `Version.has` before you use a newer feature. |
| **Incompatible** | A range in the descriptor does not agree with this installation. | Read the card. Correct the range, or update the game or Viewpoint. |
| **Needs an update** | The addon uses an internal member that Viewpoint has removed. | Read the card. It names the replacement. |

## Old jars

A jar that you compile for API 1.0 loads in all 1.x versions.

---

# Order

> What the order of the Active column controls, and how requirements and conflicts limit it.

The Active column is a list. The top of the list is first. The player drags a card to move it. Viewpoint saves the
order, and which packages are on, in the settings file of Viewpoint (`Zomboid/viewpoint-live.properties`, the key
`addons.active`). Edit it only with the game closed.

## What the order controls

| For | The order controls |
| --- | --- |
| **Hook handlers** | The handlers of one hook run from top to bottom when the game method starts, and from bottom to top when it ends. A handler that skips or replaces the call stops the handlers below it. |
| **Resource packs** | When two packs change the same sprite, state or tile, the pack nearer the top wins. |
| **Legacy model packs** | They are resource packs. The same rule applies. |
| **Camera layers** | The layers add together in this order. |
| **Claims** | Only one addon at a time holds the camera, the view, the cursor, the shot resolver or the reticle. The addon nearer the top wins. The others wait. Their cards show who holds the claim. |
| **Model and attachment providers** | When several providers answer for the same sprite, Viewpoint asks them in this order. The first that answers wins. Then come the resource packs, then the art of the game. Attachment providers are asked in this order too, and Viewpoint draws every answer. |
| **Sway and extension points** | The sway of the addons, and the contributions to an extension point, come in this order. |
| **Shader snippets** | The snippets of the addons run in this order at a point of a shader. |
| **Shaderpacks** | Nothing. Shaderpacks are not in the Active column. Only `base=` in a descriptor puts one pack on another. |
| **All other services** | Nothing. Two addons that use different services do not depend on their order. |

Viewpoint does not change the order for you. A package is in the correct position only if the player put it there.

## Requirements and conflicts

- `requires=example.core@1.0`: `example.core` must be **Active**, at version 1.0 or later, with the same major
  version. Until it is, the player cannot switch your addon on. Viewpoint names the missing package. If the player
  switches `example.core` off, Viewpoint first asks to switch off the addons that require it.
- `conflicts=other.lean`: the two packages cannot be active at the same time. Viewpoint tells the player which one is
  active.
- A requirement does not set the position of a package in the list.
- A cycle of `requires` is refused.

## Hook order

When the game calls a hooked method:

1. The `Before` handlers run from top to bottom. They stop at the first handler that skips or replaces the call.
2. The handlers below that handler are *pre-empted*. Their `Before` and `After` do not run. The card counts them.
3. The game method runs, if no handler skipped it.
4. The `After` handlers run from bottom to top. The pre-empted handlers do not run in this step.

Viewpoint keeps a copy of the handler list from the start of the call. A veto or a new order during the call does not
change which `After` handlers run for that call. See [Managed patching](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/managed-patching.md).

## The first position

When the player switches a package on, it goes to the top of the Active column. The player can then drag it to a
different position.

---

# View state

> Read where Viewpoint's view is, what it shows and where the crosshair points, one time each frame.

`ViewState` is a snapshot of Viewpoint's view. You can read it. You cannot change the view with it. To change the view, use
[camera layers](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/camera-layers.md). To follow the aim and the shots, use [aim & shots](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/aim-and-shots.md).

No permission is necessary.

## The record

`viewpoint.api.view.ViewState` is an immutable record. You can keep it, and you can give it to a different thread.

| Member | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `on()` | `boolean` | `true` when Viewpoint's view shows, in first or third person. `false` when the game's isometric view shows. |
| `mode()` | `ViewMode` | `FIRST_PERSON`, `THIRD_PERSON` or `ISOMETRIC`. `on()` is the same as `mode() != ISOMETRIC`. |
| `eye()` | `EyePose` | The position of the view's eye in world coordinates, and its direction. |
| `fov()` | `float` | The vertical field of view, in degrees. |
| `crosshair()` | `Ray` | The line from the eye through the crosshair. |
| `terrainHeight(x, y)` | `OptionalDouble` | The ground height at a point, as world `z`. Empty if Viewpoint has no height for the point, for example when terrain relief is off. |
| `versions()` | `Versions` | The game build, the Viewpoint version and the API version, as text. |
| `freeCamera()` | `boolean` | `true` while a free camera has the view. |
| `cursorCaptured()` | `boolean` | `true` while Viewpoint holds the cursor for the view. |
| `sceneOrigin()` | `Vec3` | The point of the world that is the zero of the scene. See [Scene origin](#scene-origin). |
| `crosshairHit()` | `Optional<Vec3>` | The point in the world where the line of the crosshair meets something. See [What the view points at](#what-the-view-points-at). |
| `cursorHit()` | `Optional<Vec3>` | The point in the world that the picture shows under the free cursor. See [What the view points at](#what-the-view-points-at). |

`EyePose` has `x`, `y`, `z`, and `yaw` and `pitch` in degrees. `Ray` has an origin and a unit direction, each as three
numbers. `Vec3` has `x`, `y` and `z`.

The coordinates are the game's world coordinates. The game's Lua and Java use the same coordinates. The axes are: `x`
east and `y` south, in squares, and `z` up, in storeys. One storey is the side of a square multiplied by √6.

## Listen

```java title="ViewPart.java"
public final class ViewPart {
    private final AddonContext ctx;

    ViewPart(AddonContext ctx) {
        this.ctx = ctx;
    }

    void start() {
        ctx.view().listen(state -> {
            if (state.on()) {
                state.terrainHeight(state.eye().x(), state.eye().y())
                        .ifPresent(h -> System.out.println("ground under the eye: " + h));
            }
        });
    }
}
```

`ctx.view().listen(ViewListener)` gives a `Registration`. Viewpoint closes it when the addon goes off.

Viewpoint calls `onFrame(ViewState)` of the listener on the **main thread**:

- one time each frame while the view is on;
- one more time when the view goes off.

Viewpoint calls it after it reads the game for that frame. Thus the state agrees with the frame that Viewpoint draws.

## Ask at any time

`ctx.view().state()` gives the latest `ViewState`. Call it on the main thread. Use it when you have your own trigger,
for example a key. Viewpoint builds the state only while a listener exists or someone asked for it in the last two
seconds. The first call, or the first call after a pause, gives `null`, and the next frame has the state.

## What the view points at

Viewpoint reads both points from the picture that it draws. Each point is the surface that the player sees there, with its
height in `z`. Each point is one or two frames old.

| Point | Has a value | Is empty |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crosshairHit()` | While Viewpoint holds the cursor for the view (`cursorCaptured()`), on foot, or seated in first person. In third person, a seated player must aim. | On the sky. On the vehicle of a seated player. With a free camera. While the cursor is free. |
| `cursorHit()` | While the cursor is free in first person. | On the sky. While the cursor moves. While Viewpoint holds the cursor. |

Thus use one point or the other, by `cursorCaptured()`, to know what the player clicks on. To know the direction of the
view, use `eye()`: `yaw()` is 0 to the east and 90 to the south, and `pitch()` is positive up. Neither point gives the
direction of the surface.

## Scene origin

Viewpoint draws the world relative to a point near the player, the scene origin. This keeps the numbers small. A position
that you read from a draw callback or a shader is relative to this point. To keep something fixed to the world, add
`sceneOrigin()` back to the position. Without it, a pattern moves when the player walks.

## Terrain height

`terrainHeight(x, y)` reads Viewpoint's terrain relief. This is the ground that Viewpoint draws. The call is fast. It reads
the relief that is current when you call, not the one of the frame of the state. Thus a state that you keep does not hold the
ground, and the answer can change if the relief changes. It is empty for a number that is not finite.

The value is correct only where terrain relief is on. If the player switches relief off, the result is empty. Then use
the floor height of the game.

> **Note**
>
> The game's Lua can read the same state through `Viewpoint.Addons`. See [Lua mirror](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/lua-mirror.md). On the render
> thread, a draw callback gets the matrices and sizes of the frame in a `FrameView`. See
> [Draw callbacks](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/draw-callbacks.md) (planned).

---

# Settings & keys

> Write your settings in a file. Viewpoint shows the page, keeps the values and binds the keys.

You do not draw or save the settings of your addon. You write them in `settings.properties`. Viewpoint then:

- shows the settings behind the cog on the card of the addon, while it is active;
- keeps the values;
- lets the player bind the keys again.

No permission is necessary. Name the file in the descriptor: `settings=settings.properties`.

## The file

```properties title="settings.properties"
schemaVersion=1

enabled.type=toggle
enabled.label=Lean with the camera
enabled.default=true
enabled.apply=live

angle.type=number
angle.label=Angle
angle.default=12
angle.min=0
angle.max=30
angle.step=1
angle.unit=degrees
angle.shownWhen=enabled
angle.enabledWhen=enabled

side.type=choice
side.label=Side
side.choices=left,right,both
side.default=both
side.apply=activate

leanKey.type=key
leanKey.label=Lean
leanKey.default=Q
```

Each setting is a group of keys that start with the name of the setting. A name is `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*`. A file has at
most 64 settings and is at most 64 KiB, in UTF-8. A label has at most 80 characters, a unit 16, and a choice 40.
Viewpoint takes out the characters that the player cannot see or that change the order of the text, and it writes `##` as
`#`.

If the file is wrong, Viewpoint does not start the addon and lists every problem together.

| Key | For | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<name>.type` | All | `toggle`, `number`, `choice` or `key`. |
| `<name>.label` | All | The text on the row. |
| `<name>.default` | All | The value before the player changes it. |
| `<name>.apply` | All | When a change has an effect: `live`, `activate` or `restart`. The default is `live`. |
| `<name>.shownWhen` | All | The row shows only while this condition is true. |
| `<name>.enabledWhen` | All | The player can change the row only while this condition is true. |
| `<name>.lua` | All | `true` lets the game's Lua read the value (see [Lua mirror](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/lua-mirror.md)). The default is `false`. |
| `<name>.min`, `.max`, `.step`, `.unit` | `number` | The range of the slider, its step, and a unit after the value. |
| `<name>.choices` | `choice` | The values, with commas between them. |

### `apply`

| Value | When your code gets the new value |
| --- | --- |
| `live` | At once, through `onChange`. |
| `activate` | When the addon is switched on the next time. The row tells the player. |
| `restart` | When the game starts the next time. The row tells the player. |

### Conditions

`shownWhen` and `enabledWhen` take one of these:

- the name of a toggle: `enabled`;
- the name of a toggle with `!` before it: `!enabled`;
- a choice and one of its values: `side=left`.

### `schemaVersion`

This is the version of your file, a whole number from 1 to 1000. Viewpoint keeps it with the values. If the kept values come from a newer
`schemaVersion` than the installed addon has, the page is **read-only**. This occurs when the player goes back to an
older release. Then the older addon cannot write over the values of the newer one.

## Where the values are

Viewpoint keeps the values as `addon.<encoded id>.<name>` in `viewpoint-live.properties`. The encoded id writes `.` and
`-` as `_`. For the id `example.lean` and the setting `angle`, the key is `addon.example_lean.angle`. **Reset** on the
addon's settings page sets the defaults again. See [Package kinds](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/package-kinds.md#the-encoded-id).

## Read the values

```java title="SettingsPart.java"
AddonSettings settings = ctx.settings();

boolean on = settings.toggle("enabled");
double angle = settings.number("angle");
String side = settings.choice("side");

settings.onChange("angle", () -> {
    System.out.println("angle is now " + settings.number("angle"));
});
```

- `toggle`, `number` and `choice` read the current value.
- Call these methods on the main thread only. A call from another thread, or after the addon is off, gets an `IllegalStateException`.
- If the name is not in the file, or the type is not correct, your code gets an `IllegalArgumentException`.
- `onChange(name, Runnable)` gives a `Registration`. The callback runs on the main thread, after Viewpoint keeps the value.
- A setting with `apply=activate` or `apply=restart` never calls `onChange` while the addon runs.

## Settings pages

Each addon with settings has a page in the settings window. The player opens it with the cog on the card of the addon,
while the addon is active. The page shows your settings as rows. You do not draw it. If you want more than the rows of the file, your addon can build the
page from subtabs, sections, buttons and value rows:

- a **subtab** is a part of the page, with a title at the top of the page. The player clicks the title to see the rows of that
  subtab;
- a **section** is a group of rows with a title;
- a **setting row** shows a setting from `settings.properties`;
- a **button** has a label, and its callback runs on the main thread;
- a **value row** shows a value of your addon. Viewpoint reads it on the main thread when the page is open.

```java title="SettingsPart.java"
settings.page()
        .tab("Lean")
        .section("Camera")
        .setting("enabled")
        .setting("angle")
        .section("Tools")
        .button("Reset the lean", () -> lean.reset())
        .value("Lean now", () -> lean.degrees() + " degrees")
        .tab("Keys")
        .setting("leanKey");
```

`ctx.settings().page()` gives the same page at each call, so a second call adds rows to it. The methods return the page.

- Call the methods on the main thread only. A call after the addon is off gets an `IllegalStateException`.
- A page has at most 100 rows. Each subtab and each section is a row too. A section title and a label have at most 80
  characters, a subtab title and a button 40, a value 200. Viewpoint cleans the texts as it does the labels of the file, and
  cuts them.
- A page has at most 8 subtabs. A subtab holds the rows that follow it, up to the next subtab. Sections divide a subtab as
  they divide a page. Rows that come before the first subtab go on a first subtab, **General**.
- `setting(name)` gives an `IllegalArgumentException` for a name that is not in the file, or for one that the page already shows.
- A setting that you do not put on the page follows the sections, in a group **Other settings**. On a page with subtabs,
  **Other settings** is the last subtab. The player can always reach it, a key too.
- A button runs at the start of the next frame, on the main thread, after the player clicks it. At most eight clicks wait. A
  second click on the same button within 0.3 seconds is a double click: the callback runs once. A callback that throws
  suspends the addon, as any handler does.
- Viewpoint asks for the text of a value row about ten times a second, only while the page is open and drawn. The text is
  short: it is a value, not a log. All the value rows of a page get 2 milliseconds a round. When they take more, the rows
  that are left keep their last text and are read first in the next round, so a slow row is shown late.

A page has no drawing code of your own. Keep the texts short. If your addon builds no page, the player sees the settings of the
file in the order of the file.

## Keys

A setting of type `key` is a key binding. It shows in the group of your addon, **Addons**, under the id of your addon.
The group never has the name that your addon chooses, so it cannot look like one of Viewpoint's. The player binds the key
again with the same editor as for Viewpoint's keys.

Your key only listens. When the player presses it, the game still gets the press. Your addon cannot take a key from the
game.

The default of a key must be free. If it is one of these, the key starts **unbound** and the card of your addon says so:

- Esc, or Shift, Ctrl or Alt alone;
- a key that the game binds;
- a key that Viewpoint binds, or that a different addon binds.

If the player has saved a key that a different binding now holds too, Viewpoint keeps it and says so on the card. The
default keys of an addon are shown to the player before the first run. An update that changes one is shown as a change.

```java title="SettingsPart.java"
KeyAction lean = settings.key("leanKey");

lean.onPress(() -> System.out.println("lean pressed"));
lean.onRelease(() -> System.out.println("lean released"));
```

| `KeyAction` member | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `onPress(Runnable)` | Runs on the main thread when the key goes down. Gives a `Registration`. |
| `onRelease(Runnable)` | Runs on the main thread when the key goes up. Gives a `Registration`. |
| `isDown()` | `true` while the key is down. |

A key does not operate in these conditions:

- a text box has the focus;
- Viewpoint's window uses the keyboard;
- the game's own UI uses the keyboard.

> **Note**
>
> Viewpoint makes the key bindings when the addon goes on, and removes them when it goes off. Viewpoint keeps the key that
> the player set. It uses that key again the next time.

---

# Lua mirror

> Read the view state and the settings that an addon shares, from the game's Lua.

`Viewpoint.Addons` is a mirror for reading. A Lua mod can read two things: the view state, and the settings that an addon
shares. Viewpoint changes nothing through these functions.

To call the Java functions of your own addon from Lua, use exports. See [Lua exports](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/lua-exports.md). The
exports of an addon are in `Viewpoint.Addons["<id>"]`. The functions on this page are in `Viewpoint.Addons` itself.

## The functions

| Function | Gives |
| --- | --- |
| `Viewpoint.Addons.viewState()` | A table with the fields below. `nil` the first time, and after a pause of two seconds without a call. |
| `Viewpoint.Addons.terrainHeight(x, y)` | The ground height at the point, or `nil`. `nil` also for a number that is not finite. |
| `Viewpoint.Addons.setting(addonId, name)` | The current value of one setting of one addon: a boolean, a number or a string. `nil` if the addon is off, the setting does not exist, or the addon did not share it (see below). |

Viewpoint builds the view state only while it is asked for. Call `viewState()` each frame to keep it. The first call, or the
first call after a pause of two seconds, answers `nil`, and the next frame has the table.

An addon shares a setting with `<name>.lua=true` in its `settings.properties`. Every other setting answers `nil`. Any mod
can read a shared setting, so share only what you want every mod to see.

The table of the view state:

```lua
local v = Viewpoint.Addons.viewState()

if v and v.on then
    print(v.mode)               -- "FIRST_PERSON" or "THIRD_PERSON"
    print(v.eye.x, v.eye.y, v.eye.z, v.eye.yaw, v.eye.pitch)
    print(v.fov)
    print(v.crosshair.x, v.crosshair.y, v.crosshair.z)         -- the ray's origin
    print(v.crosshair.dx, v.crosshair.dy, v.crosshair.dz)      -- its direction
    print(v.versions.game, v.versions.viewpoint, v.versions.api)
    print(v.freeCamera, v.cursorCaptured)
    print(v.sceneOrigin.x, v.sceneOrigin.y, v.sceneOrigin.z)
    if v.crosshairHit then print(v.crosshairHit.x, v.crosshairHit.y, v.crosshairHit.z) end -- nil if it meets nothing
    if v.cursorHit then print(v.cursorHit.x, v.cursorHit.y, v.cursorHit.z) end             -- under the free cursor
end
```

The fields and units are the same as in [`ViewState`](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/view-state.md). The coordinates are the game's world
coordinates.

## Rules

- Call the functions on the main thread. The game's Lua runs there.
- There are no callbacks. Ask each frame, or when your own trigger occurs.
- You do not need an addon. The Lua of all mods can call these functions.
- `setting` gives the value that the player has set now. This includes a value that has an effect only at the next
  enable.
- The table that you get is a copy. If you change it, nothing changes in Viewpoint.
- `Viewpoint.Addons` is one table that every mod shares, and it also holds the [exports](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/lua-exports.md) of the addons by
  their ids. Lua lets a mod write to it. A mod that does can change what a different mod reads from it. Viewpoint does
  not protect the table.

---

# Lua exports

> An addon gives some of its Java functions to Lua, with names, types and a time limit.

An addon can give some functions of its Java to Lua. The Lua of **any** mod can call them. You mark a function with
`@LuaExport`. The card of the addon lists the functions, and says what they can reach.

**Permission:** `lua`. Without it, the addon does not start.

```properties title="addon.properties"
permissions=lua
lua.globals=Fireworks
```

## Mark a function

Put `@LuaExport` on a public static method. Or put it on a class: then all the public static methods that the class
declares are exports.

```java title="Fireworks.java"
@LuaExport
public final class Fireworks {
    private Fireworks() {}

    public static int launch(String color, int count) {
        // ...
        return count;
    }

    @LuaExport(name = "stop")
    public static void cancelAll() {
        // ...
    }
}
```

`name` is the name that Lua uses: for a method, in place of its Java name; for a class, in place of its simple name.
Lua has no overloads. If two methods have the same Lua name, Viewpoint refuses both.

A mod that you port from ZombieBuddy can keep its `@Exposer.LuaClass` classes: Viewpoint reads them as exports of
their public static methods. See [Migrating from ZombieBuddy](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/migrating-from-zombiebuddy.md).

A method that is not public and static is not an export. The instance methods of a class are never exports.

## The names

Lua finds each export as `Viewpoint.Addons["<id>"].<Class>.<method>`:

```lua
local n = Viewpoint.Addons["example.fireworks"].Fireworks.launch("red", 3)
```

If `lua.globals` lists the name of a class, Lua also finds the class under that global name:

```lua
local n = Fireworks.launch("red", 3)
```

Viewpoint **refuses a global**, and writes the reason in `console.txt`, in these cases:

- the global already exists when your addon starts;
- another mod sets the global at the top level of its Lua. A statement in an `if` or `do` of a file counts, because it
  runs when the file loads. A `local` does not. `X = ...`, `X.y = ...`, `function X()`, `_G.X = ...` and
  `_G["X"] = ...` all set `X`.
- Viewpoint could not read the Lua of another mod completely.

A name in `lua.globals` that no exported class has is written in `console.txt` too, and the addon starts.

A refused global does not stop the addon. The name `Viewpoint.Addons["<id>"]` always works. Write your Lua with that name
if you must not depend on a global.

> **Caution**
>
> Viewpoint cannot see a name that another mod makes with `_G[expression]`, `rawset`, `setfenv` or `loadstring`.

## The types

A function can take and give only these types. Any other type refuses the function. The other functions of the addon
stay.

| Type | In Lua |
| --- | --- |
| `boolean`, `Boolean` | A boolean. |
| `byte`, `short`, `int`, `long` (and their boxes) | A whole number in the range of the type. `long` goes up to 2^53: Lua numbers are `double`. A `long` result past 2^53 is an error in the Lua that called, not a rounded number. |
| `float`, `double` (and their boxes) | A number. A `float` result is the number that it prints as (`0.1f` is `0.1`). |
| `char`, `Character` | A string of one character. |
| `String` | A string. A string passes as it is. It can hold a NUL byte, `..` or anything else. |
| `LuaTable` | A table. See [Tables](#tables). |
| `LuaHandle` | A number. See [Handles](#handles). |
| A game class of the list below | An object of the game, as it is. |
| `void` | Nothing. Only as a result. |

A `nil` of Lua gives `null` for a box, a `String`, a `LuaTable`, a `LuaHandle` or a game class. For a primitive type it is
an error.

The game classes that a function can pass are: `IsoPlayer`, `IsoZombie`, `IsoGameCharacter`, `IsoGridSquare`,
`IsoObject`, `InventoryItem`, `HandWeapon` and `BaseVehicle`. The list can grow. Ask for a class that you need.

A function cannot use `Object`, an array, a list, a map, a stream, a reader, a writer or a class of your own. A varargs
function (`String...`) is an array, so it is refused.

### Tables

`LuaTable` is a wrapper. It is not the table of the game. It reads and writes these values: `Boolean`, `Double` (every Lua
number), `String` and `LuaTable`. A key is a string or a whole number. A Lua value of another type (a function, an object
of the game) reads as `null`. A value of another type that you set is an error.

```java
public static LuaTable summary(LuaTable input) {
    LuaTable out = input.newTable();
    out.set("count", input.length());
    out.set("name", "summary");

    return out;
}
```

A `LuaTable` is good only while the call runs. Do not keep it.

### Handles

Lua cannot hold an object of your addon. Give it a handle instead. `ctx.handle(object)` makes a `LuaHandle`. Lua sees a
number. When Lua gives the number back to a function that takes a `LuaHandle`, Viewpoint finds the object again.

```java
public static LuaHandle open(String name) {
    return context.handle(new Session(name));
}

public static void close(LuaHandle session) {
    session.release();
}
```

- A number is chosen at random from the whole numbers that Lua holds exactly, so Lua cannot find a handle by counting. A
  number is not used for two handles in the life of the game, and the number of a handle of an earlier start of your addon
  names nothing in the next. The Lua of all the mods is one trust domain: a number that a mod has can be given to any
  function of your addon that takes a handle, so do not use a handle as a secret.
- `ctx.handle`, `release()` and the methods of a `LuaTable` work on the main thread of the game only. From another thread
  they throw an `IllegalStateException`.
- An addon can have 4096 handles at one time. More is an error. Call `release()` for the ones that you do not need.
- A handle that you released, a handle of another addon, and a number that no handle has are errors in the Lua that uses
  them.
- When the addon goes off, Viewpoint clears all its handles.

## The calls

- Lua calls an export on the main thread only. A call from another thread is an error.
- Viewpoint counts each call and adds its time to `addon.<id>.mainMs`. The Performance tab shows the sum.
- If an export **throws**, Viewpoint suspends the addon and gives a Lua error. Do not let an export throw for a wrong
  argument of the caller: check the arguments, and return a result that tells the caller.
- Treat every argument as if a stranger sent it. Any mod can call your exports. For a path, use [`AddonFiles`](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/files.md).
  For an address, use [`AddonDownloads`](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/downloads.md). Their rules apply to an argument from Lua too.

## The errors that Lua sees

An error is a Lua error. A Lua author can use `pcall` to catch it. The text names the function and what to change:

| The text | The cause |
| --- | --- |
| `argument 1 of Viewpoint.Addons["x"].C.m must be a whole number, not a string` | The type of an argument is wrong. |
| `... must be a whole number from -128 to 127` | The number is out of range for the type. |
| `... must not be nil` | A `nil` for a primitive type. |
| `... takes 2 arguments, not 1` | The number of arguments is wrong. |
| `... must be a handle number that this addon made and has not released` | The handle is gone, or is not from this addon. |
| `... can only be called on the main thread of the game` | A call from another thread. |
| `... failed: <the exception>. The addon is suspended` | The export threw. |
| `... addon x is suspended because one of its functions failed` | A call after a throw. |
| `... addon x is off` | The addon is off. A function that Lua kept in a variable gives this error too. |

## At the start of the game

A mod runs its top-level Lua while the game loads. The exports must be there before that. So at the first Lua start of the
game, Viewpoint waits for your addon. It checks the addon and starts it, and then it installs the exports. This wait is
**about 5 seconds** for all the addons together. Viewpoint tests the time between the starts of addons, so a slow
`enable` can pass it. An addon that needs the wait:

- holds the `lua` permission, and
- the player has it on, with the consent for its jar.

While it waits, Viewpoint writes "Viewpoint is checking N addons" in `console.txt` and shows it as a notice.

If an addon is not ready after 5 seconds, it starts at the first frame. This is also true when Viewpoint could not
finish finding the packages in time: then every addon with exports is late. Its exports are then there **after** the top-level
Lua of the mods ran. The card of the addon says "Its Lua functions came late at this start." A Lua mod can call your
functions later, from an event.

The game starts its Lua again at some times: when the player joins or leaves a server, changes an option, loads a world
with another set of mods, or returns to the menu. Each time, the Lua is new and empty, and Viewpoint installs the exports
again. This second time there is no wait: the addon is on already.

> **Note**
>
> You do not need to do anything for the second start. Do not keep a Lua function from an earlier start: after a restart
> of the Lua it is not in the new Lua.

## When the addon goes off

Each export becomes a stub. It gives the error "addon x is off". Viewpoint clears the handles. The class loader of the
addon can then unload. Do not keep a `LuaTable` or a `LuaHandle` in a static field of a class that the game keeps.

---

# Files

> AddonFiles gives an addon one folder, with name rules, a quota, and results on the main thread.

Use `AddonFiles` to keep files. Do not use `java.io.File` or `java.nio.file`: they make the label **Red**.
`AddonFiles` gives your addon one folder with a quota. It gives the results on the main thread.

**Permission:** `files`. Without it, each call gives a `SecurityException` to your code.

```properties
permissions=files
files.quotaMiB=16
```

## The folder

Your folder is `Zomboid/viewpoint-addons/<id>/`. You cannot name a file outside it. Viewpoint never loads code from this
folder.
