On the addon's **Files** tab, the player can:

- open the folder;
- see its size and the download log;
- delete it.

## Use it

```java title="FilesPart.java"
AddonFiles files = ctx.files();

files.read("counter.txt")
        .then(bytes -> {
            int n = Integer.parseInt(new String(bytes, StandardCharsets.US_ASCII));
            files.write("counter.txt", Integer.toString(n + 1).getBytes(StandardCharsets.US_ASCII));
        })
        .otherwise(error -> files.write("counter.txt", "1".getBytes(StandardCharsets.US_ASCII)));
```

The first time, the file is not there: the read fails, and `otherwise` writes the first number. A test compiles this code and
runs it against the real `AddonFiles`.

| Method | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `read(name)` | `Pending<byte[]>`. Fails if the file does not exist. |
| `write(name, bytes)` | `Pending<Void>`. Viewpoint copies `bytes` at the call. If the game stops during a write, the old file stays complete. |
| `delete(name)` | `Pending<Void>`. A file that is not there is not an error. |
| `exists(name)` | `Pending<Boolean>`. |
| `list(prefix)` | `Pending<List<String>>`. The names that start with the prefix, in order. A file that the player put in the folder, with a name that is not a valid name, is not in the list. |
| `usage()` | `Pending<AddonFiles.Usage>`. The `bytes` and the `files` in the folder, and the `quotaBytes`. |

### `Pending<T>`

Viewpoint does the disk work on a different thread. `Pending<T>` gives you the result.

| Member | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `then(Consumer<T>)` | Runs if the work is successful. Gives the same `Pending`. |
| `otherwise(Consumer<Throwable>)` | Runs if the work fails. Gives the same `Pending`. |
| `isDone()` | `true` when the work is complete. |

The callbacks run on the **main thread**, in a frame after the work is complete. You can chain `then` and `otherwise`. If
the addon goes off before a callback runs, Viewpoint does not run that callback.

## Names

- Use lower-case letters, digits, `-` and `_`.
- Use `/` to put a file in a subfolder. Keep the names short and the subfolders few.
- Use one extension from this list: `png`, `jpg`, `json`, `txt`, `csv`, `properties`, `ogg`, `wav`, `obj`, `mtl`,
  `bin`, `dat`.

If Viewpoint does not accept a name, the call throws `IllegalArgumentException` immediately. You get no `Pending`. Use a
simple lower-case name with an extension from the list.

## Limits

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| The folder | 64 MiB by default. A larger `files.quotaMiB` needs the player's consent. |
| One file | 16 MiB |
| Files and folders together | 1,000. A folder that a delete leaves empty goes with it. |

If a write goes over a limit, its `Pending` fails with an error. Viewpoint does not delete files to make space.

Viewpoint also limits what waits. At most 256 calls wait for their result, and at most 32 MiB of data is in transfer (a
write that has not finished, or a read that you have not taken). A call over a limit throws `IllegalStateException`; make
the next call in the callback of an earlier one. The errors name your file, never a path on the player's computer.

Call `AddonFiles` and its `Pending` on the main thread. From any other thread a call throws `IllegalStateException`.

A link, a junction or a special file in your folder is not followed. A call that meets one fails. Your addon cannot make
one.

---

# Downloads

> AddonDownloads gets a file from the internet. The player accepts each download.

Use `AddonDownloads` to get a file from the internet. Do not open network connections yourself: `java.net` makes the
label **Red**. Viewpoint asks the player **each time**, and shows the full address.

**Permission:** `downloads`, with the hosts in `downloads.hosts`. The file goes into your [`AddonFiles`](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/files.md)
folder, so you also need the `files` permission.

```properties
permissions=files,downloads
files.quotaMiB=16
downloads.hosts=github.com,objects.githubusercontent.com
```

## Ask for a download

```java title="DownloadPart.java"
DownloadRequest request = DownloadRequest.get("https://github.com/example/lean/releases/download/v1/extra.dat", "extra.dat")
        .declaredBytes(120_000);

ctx.downloads().request(request)
        .then(result -> System.out.println("[Sample] " + result.status() + " from " + result.finalHost()))
        .otherwise(error -> System.out.println("[Sample] " + error.getMessage()));
```

A test compiles this code against the API and runs it in an addon.

- Use an `https` URL with a host name: no user name, no port, no address of numbers, no hidden character. Viewpoint
  refuses the others with an `IllegalArgumentException` at the call.
- Use a host that is in `downloads.hosts`. If the server redirects to a different host, put that host in the list also.
  Viewpoint follows at most three redirects, and judges each one as it judges the first address.
- Give the file a name with the same rules as [`AddonFiles`](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/files.md#names).
- Set `declaredBytes` to the size of the file. The player sees it.

`request(DownloadRequest)` gives a `Pending<DownloadResult>`. Its callbacks run on the main thread. A refusal is not an
error. It is a result with a `status`.

| `DownloadResult` member | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `status()` | One of the values below. |
| `name()` | The name of the file in your folder. |
| `bytes()` | The size that Viewpoint wrote. |
| `finalHost()` | The host that sent the file, after the redirects. Empty if no host answered. |
| `reason()` | Why the download did not end in `OK`, in one sentence. Empty for `OK`. |

| `status()` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `OK` | The file is in your folder. |
| `DENIED` | The player did not accept the download. |
| `DENIED_SESSION` | The player did not accept too many times. The addon cannot ask again in this session. |
| `NOT_SHOWN` | Viewpoint could not show the prompt. |
| `TOO_LARGE` | The file is larger than the limit. |
| `FAILED` | The download did not complete. |

## What the player sees

Each call shows a dialog. The dialog shows:

- the name and the label of the addon;
- the **full URL**, with emphasis on the host;
- the destination: `viewpoint-addons/<id>/<name>`;
- the size, if you set `declaredBytes`.

The player clicks **Deny** or **Accept**. Esc is a Deny. Deny works at once. Accept is grey for the first half second
after the player first sees the question, and takes a click only after the pointer has rested on it for a moment. If
several addons ask, the window says "Question 2 of 3", and each question starts again. The address is shown in full, with
the host in colour; a long address scrolls.

If the player does not answer in 60 seconds, the result is `DENIED`. That includes a question that the game could not show
yet (the setup or a crash report was on the screen).

The player answers with the **mouse**. A player with only a controller cannot accept a download in this version: the
question denies itself after 60 seconds, and your addon gets `DENIED`.

Ask only when the player needs the file. If your addon asks too frequently, Viewpoint shows fewer prompts:

- One question of your addon waits at a time, and three in all. Another call gets `NOT_SHOWN`.
- After a denial, or after a question that nobody answered, a call in the next 30 seconds gets `DENIED` at once.
- After the player denies three questions, your addon gets `DENIED_SESSION` until the game starts again. A question that nobody
  answered is not one of the three.
- The player answers with the mouse. If the game cannot show the question, you get `NOT_SHOWN` at once.

## Limits

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| One file | 256 MiB, and it must also fit in your files quota. |
| The quota | Viewpoint holds it for the file as the size is known: at once for a size you declare or the server says, else as the bytes come. If the quota ends, the status is `TOO_LARGE`. Declare `declaredBytes`. |
| At a time | At most 3 accepted downloads at a time: the one that runs and the ones that wait for it. The next gets `FAILED`. |
| One download | 10 minutes in all once it starts, whatever the speed of the server. The time that it waits for the one before is not counted. |
| Redirects | 3 |
| Request | A plain `GET`. You cannot set headers, a body, a method or cookies. |

## Errors

| You see | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SecurityException` | The descriptor does not have the `downloads` permission. | Add `downloads` to `permissions`, and the hosts to `downloads.hosts`. |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | The address, its host or the name is not accepted. | Use an `https` URL on a host from `downloads.hosts`, and a name by the rules of `AddonFiles`. |
| `IllegalStateException` | You called from a thread that is not the main thread. | Call `AddonDownloads` on the main thread. |
| `FAILED` | The download stopped, the host has no public address, or it took too long. `reason()` says. | Read `reason()` and `console.txt`. |
| `FAILED` after a redirect | The server redirects to a host that is not in `downloads.hosts`. | Add that host to `downloads.hosts`. The player must then give consent again. |
| `TOO_LARGE` | The file is larger than the limit or your quota. | Use a smaller file, or ask for a larger `files.quotaMiB`. |

The addon's **Files** tab shows each download: the file, the address, and the time.

## What Viewpoint does not promise

- Viewpoint connects only to public addresses: not to the player's own computer or network. It looks up the host before it
  connects, and the connection looks it up again. The Java cache of names keeps the answer between the two for 30 seconds. If
  the player's Java runs with that cache off, a server that answers a different address the second time can still reach a
  private address. The protection that remains is that the player sees every host.
- The player reads the address. Two host names that look alike in the font (`rn` and `m`) are for the player to tell apart.
- A network that only has IPv6, and translates the names of IPv4 hosts (NAT64), cannot download: Viewpoint cannot tell
  which address such a name leads to. The status is `FAILED`, and the reason says so. Few player computers are on such a
  network.
- Viewpoint does not check what the file is. It keeps the file under the rules of `AddonFiles`, and never loads code from it.

---

# Assets

> AddonAssets loads the models, textures, sounds and data of an addon into memory pools with limits.

Use `AddonAssets` for files in your package: a model, a texture, a sound, a data table. It uses the same loaders as a
resource pack. Thus the same limits apply. No permission is necessary.

## Where the assets are

Set the same four keys in the descriptor as a resource pack. `models` is the path of a manifest. The other three are
folders. Use a version 2 manifest. See [Format](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/resource-packs/format.md#models) and
[Model states](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/resource-packs/model-states.md). Version 1 is deprecated.

```properties
models=models/manifest.txt
tiles=tiles
sounds=sounds
data=data
```

Each path must be in your mod's folder. If it is not, the card shows an error.

## The four kinds

| Kind | Call | Files | Pool |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Models | `ctx.assets().models()` | OBJ models with their art, put on sprites by a model manifest | `memory.packMiB` |
| Textures | `ctx.assets().textures()` | PNG images in the folder of the manifest | `memory.packMiB` |
| Sounds | `ctx.assets().sounds()` | `ogg` and `wav` files | `memory.soundMiB` |
| Data | `ctx.assets().data()` | Files read as bytes, 16 MiB maximum each | `memory.addonDataMiB` |

Code does not load tile textures. To replace the game's tile art, use the `tiles` folder. See
[Tiles](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/resource-packs/tiles.md). To choose a model with code, use a provider. See
[Model providers](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/model-providers.md).

## Use them

```java title="AssetsPart.java"
AddonAssets assets = ctx.assets();

assets.data().read("table.csv").then(bytes -> System.out.println("table: " + bytes.length + " bytes"));

if (assets.sounds().available()) {
    assets.sounds().load("click.ogg").then(sound -> sound.play());
} else {
    System.out.println("[Sample] sound is off in this install");
}
```

A load gives a `Pending`. Its callbacks run on the main thread. Viewpoint reads or decodes the asset on a different thread.
Thus a load does not stop a frame. Call the methods of `ctx.assets()` on the main thread. A name has the same rules as the name
of a file in [Files](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/files.md): lower-case, at most four parts, and a known extension.

- `data().read(name)` gives a copy of the bytes each time. Viewpoint keeps one copy in the pool until your addon goes off.
  Two reads of one file at the same time are one read.
- `sounds().load(name)` gives a `Sound`. Viewpoint reads the length of the file from its header before it decodes it. A sound
  that decodes to more than 32 MiB, or a file whose header does not say its length, is refused and is not decoded. `play()` plays it once. `close()` gives its memory back. A sound that you do not
  close stays until your addon goes off.
- `models().manifest()` and `models().bytes()` give the path of your manifest and what your models take in the pool now.
  `textures().bytes()` gives the same for your textures. Viewpoint loads both from the manifest that `models=` names, when the
  package runs, and takes them out when it stops. You do not load them with code.

### Sounds

`sounds().available()` is `false` only when the game's sound is off. Then the card tells the player. Use
`available()` before you use a sound.

## When a pool is full

Viewpoint counts each asset in a pool, for your package. One package can hold at most **half** of a pool. If the pool is full,
or you hold half of it, Viewpoint **refuses your asset**:

- the load fails with a message that names the pool;
- the card shows the same message;
- your other assets stay loaded.

Viewpoint never removes the assets of a different package to make space for yours. See
[Assets & budgets](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/performance/assets-and-budgets.md) for the pool sizes and the estimates on the **Performance** tab.

> **Tip**
>
> Keep assets small. Load them when you need them. A texture of 4096 × 4096 pixels uses 85 MiB of video memory with its
> mipmaps.

---

# Services

> Publish a service for other addons, find the services of other addons, and add to an extension point.

`ctx.services()` lets one addon give a feature to other addons. Use it in place of a hook on the classes of another addon.
Viewpoint refuses a hook on a class of another addon.

No permission is necessary. A new `exports=` package needs the player's consent. See [Consent](#consent-and-levels).

## Publish a service

A service has an id, a type and an implementation. The type is a Java interface.

```java title="CurvesAddon.java"
public final class CurvesAddon implements Addon {
    @Override
    public void enable(AddonContext ctx) {
        ctx.services().publish("example.curves:table", CurveTable.class, new Table());
    }
}
```

`publish` gives a `Registration`. Viewpoint closes it when the addon goes off. The id of a service is the id of your
addon, a colon and a name: `example.curves:table` for the addon `example.curves`. The colon is not in the id of an addon, so
another addon cannot take your name, even an addon whose id starts like yours. The name has at most 100 characters: `a-z`,
`0-9`, `.`, `_` and `-`. An id has one publisher at a time. An addon can publish 64 services.

The type must be one of these:

- an interface of `viewpoint.api`;
- an interface in a package that you name in `exports=` in the descriptor.

```properties title="addon.properties"
exports=com.example.curves.api
```

Put the types that other addons use in one small package. Do not put your own work classes in it.

## Find a service

```java title="LeanAddon.java"
ctx.services().lookup("example.curves:table", CurveTable.class)
        .ifPresent(table -> use(table));
```

`lookup` gives an `Optional`. If the service is not there, or it was published as a different type, the result is empty. It is
not an error. Thus your addon can
work with the other addon or without it.

If you want the other addon to be there, put it in `requires`:

```properties
requires=example.curves@1.0
```

An addon that uses types from the `exports=` package of another addon must have that addon in `requires`. Viewpoint then
lets your code link to those types. Viewpoint does not let your jar hold a class of that package.

## Extension points

An extension point lets many addons add to one feature. The addon that owns the feature reads the contributions. The
other addons give them.

```java
// An addon adds its part
ctx.services().contribute("example.aim.modifiers", AimModifier.class, new MyModifier());

// The owner reads all parts, in the order of the player
for (AimModifier part : ctx.services().contributions("example.aim.modifiers", AimModifier.class)) {
    angle = part.apply(angle);
}
```

`contributions` gives the parts in the order of the Active column. The part of the addon nearer the top comes first. See
[Order](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/order.md). The id of an extension point is the choice of the addon that owns it. An addon can have 16 parts.

## Consent and levels

- A new `exports=` package or a new `requires` needs the player's consent again.
- An addon that links to another addon takes the highest level of the addons it links to. If a publisher is Red, the
  card of the consumer says **uses code of X (Red)**.
- The card of the consumer also says what each addon that it links to can do, for example **example.curves (downloads,
  files)**. A change of this is shown as a change.
- A cycle of `requires` is refused.
- When the player switches off a publisher, Viewpoint first switches off the addons that require it. The player sees a
  question before this happens.
- When a publisher is suspended, because its code threw, the addons that require it are suspended in the same step. They
  start again together when the player switches the publisher on again.
- A service of a type of `viewpoint.api` needs no `requires`. Such a service does not give the consumer a level: the player
  agreed to the publisher on its own.

> **Caution**
>
> A service is code of another author that runs in your addon's calls. Treat what it gives as untrusted.

## What you get

`lookup` and `contributions` do not give you the object of the other addon. They give an object of the same interface that
calls it for you. You can keep it. These rules apply to it:

- It works only while the registration is open. After the other addon is off, each call throws an `IllegalStateException`
  with the text "no longer there". Do not use it after that. Look up the service again when the other addon is back.
- You can call it only on the main thread. A call from another thread throws an `IllegalStateException`.
- The time of a call is the time of the addon that gave the service, not yours.
- If the code of the service throws an exception that its interface declares, you get that exception. If it throws an
  `IllegalArgumentException`, a `NullPointerException` or an `IllegalStateException`, you get the same kind of exception with the
  text. This is how a service says no to a bad argument, and it is not a fault of the addon that gave it.
- Any other exception is a strike for the addon that gave the service. Your call gets an `IllegalStateException` with the
  text of the error and no cause. At the third strike of a session, Viewpoint suspends that addon.

## Threads

Publish, look up and contribute on the main thread. A call from another thread gets an `IllegalStateException`. Calls to a service run on the thread of the caller. Viewpoint does
not move a call to another thread.

---

# Camera layers

> Move the camera with a layer that adds to Viewpoint's own motion, or take the whole camera for a short time with a claim.

An addon does not own the camera. It adds to the camera with a **layer**, or it takes the camera for a short time with a
**claim**. Use this API in place of a write to the look, the eye or the field of view.

**Permission:** `camera`.

```properties
permissions=camera
```

## Layers

A `CameraLayer` adds a small change to the camera. Many addons can have a layer at the same time. Viewpoint adds the
layers together with its own motion. The player's order decides the order of the layers. See [Order](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/order.md).

A layer has these values. Each is neutral until you set it.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Eye offset | Moves the eye, relative to the view. |
| Yaw, pitch, roll | Turns the view. |
| Lean | Leans the view to one side. |
| Field of view | A factor, and an amount to add. |

- Set the values on the main thread, once each frame. A value stays as you set it until you set it again.
- Viewpoint applies the layers in the render of the frame with the newest look of the player. Thus the camera does not
  lag. The layers work in first person and in third person.
- Set a value back to its neutral value to stop the effect, or close the layer. Viewpoint closes the layers when the addon
  goes off.

```java title="LeanPart.java"
CameraLayer layer = ctx.camera().layer();

// Each frame, on the main thread:
layer.lean(leaning ? 1.0 : 0.0)      // -1 left to 1 right
        .turn(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)          // yaw right, pitch up, roll right, in degrees
        .eye(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)           // right, up, back, in squares
        .fov(zoomed ? 0.5 : 1.0, 0.0); // a factor on the field of view, and degrees to add
```

| Method | Limits |
| --- | --- |
| `eye(right, up, back)` | All the layers together move the eye at most 2 squares each way. A square is the side of a floor tile. |
| `turn(yaw, pitch, roll)` | All the layers together turn the view at most 45 degrees each way. |
| `lean(amount)` | From -1 to 1. A full lean rolls the view by 10 degrees and moves it 0.3 squares to that side. |
| `fov(factor, degrees)` | The factor is from 0.1 to 10. The factors of the layers multiply, their degrees add. The field of view stays from 15 to 150 degrees. |
| `reset()` | Every value back to neutral. |
| `close()` | The layer goes. |

- An addon has at most 8 layers open at a time.
- A value that is not a finite number gets an `IllegalArgumentException`. A call on a closed layer, after the addon is
  off, or from a thread that is not the main thread gets an `IllegalStateException`.
- Without the `camera` permission, each call gets a `SecurityException`.
- The free camera of Viewpoint is the player's own: the layers do not move it.

## Claims

A `CameraClaim` takes the whole pose of the camera. Use it for a cut scene, a death camera or a free camera.

- Only one claim can hold the camera at a time. The addon nearer the top of the Active column wins.
- An addon that does not win waits. The card of the addon shows who holds the camera.
- While you hold the claim, you set the whole pose of the camera.
- Release the claim when you finish. Viewpoint releases the claim of an addon that it suspends. The release happens at
  the start of the next frame, and the frame that is being drawn keeps its values.

```java title="DeathCamPart.java"
CameraClaim claim = ctx.camera().claim(false); // false: only the picture moves

// Each frame while it moves, on the main thread:
claim.pose(x, y, z, yaw, pitch, 0.0) // the game's x, y and level; degrees: 0 looks east, 90 south
        .fov(70.0);                  // degrees, 15 to 150

// When it ends:
ctx.camera().look().set(yaw, pitch); // the player looks this way after the cut scene
claim.close();
```

- `claim(false)` moves only the picture. The world stays loaded, culled and heard round the player: keep the camera near
  the player. `claim(true)` is **physical**: what Viewpoint draws far off, its lights, its culling and its sound go by
  where the camera stands. The game still loads its own chunks round the player.
- Until the first `pose`, the claim draws nothing of its own: the view stays the player's.
- `held()` tells if the claim holds the camera now. A claim that waits keeps its pose, and it is drawn from as soon as it
  holds.
- An addon has one camera claim open at a time. The pitch is from -89 to 89 degrees.
- The player's own free camera of Viewpoint wins over any claim.
- While a claim holds the camera, the player's head is drawn, and the crosshair is not.

## Look, view and cursor

| Type | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `LookControl` | Add to the look of the player every frame, with look deltas: `ctx.camera().look().turn(yaw, pitch)`, in degrees, right and up. Viewpoint adds them as it reads the mouse for the next frame, while the look is the player's; it drops them while it is not. `look().set(yaw, pitch)` sets the look at the next frame, only while you hold the camera claim. |
| `LookControl`, to follow | Turn the look with something that moves, for example a car: `ctx.camera().look().follow(yaw, pitch)` once a frame, with where the car points, in degrees. The look turns by as much as the car moves, and the player keeps their own look relative to it. Viewpoint takes up each move smoothly as it reads the mouse. Use this in place of `turn` for a way that moves all the time. `stopFollowing()` stops it. |
| `ViewControl` | `ctx.camera().view().request(ViewMode.THIRD_PERSON)`: first person, third person, or the isometric view (`ISOMETRIC`). While it holds, the player's keys to switch the view wait. When you close it, the player's view comes back. |
| `CursorClaim` | `ctx.camera().cursor()`: the view lets go of the mouse, so the player can click a window of your addon. The look does not turn while it holds. |

These claims work in the same way as the camera claim: one holder, the top of the order wins, and a card shows the holder.

> **Note**
>
> These types replace the writes that older addons did with reflection. Reflection into Viewpoint is Red. A layer is Normal.
> See [Migrating from ZombieBuddy](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/migrating-from-zombiebuddy.md).

## Read the result

`ViewState` tells you if the free camera is on. See [View state](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/view-state.md).

---

# Aim & shots

> Listen to the aim and to each shot, add sway, decide the result of a shot, and draw your own reticle.

Use this API to follow the aim of the player and their shots, and to change them in a defined way.

**Permission:** `combat`.

```properties
permissions=combat
```

## When it works

These types work while the player aims a firearm with the gunplay of Viewpoint: "Gunplay Rework" is on, and the view is
first person or third person. When the gunplay is off, the game aims, and Viewpoint calls none of them.

All of them run on the main thread. Keep them short. Get them from `ctx.combat()`. Viewpoint closes what you registered when
your addon goes off.

Places and lines use the coordinates of the [view state](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/view-state.md): `x` east, `y` south, `z` up in levels, where
Viewpoint draws things. Angles are in degrees. A yaw of 0 looks east, 90 looks south.

## Listeners

| Type | When Viewpoint calls it | What you get |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AimListener` | Each update while the player aims. | `AimState`: the weapon, the origin of the aim, the yaw and pitch of the middle of the aim ring, the sway of the crosshair, the radius of the ring, the patience, the line of the crosshair, the target, and whether the crosshair is on a body that a shot would hit. |
| `ShotListener` | When Viewpoint has resolved a shot, and again when the game has dealt its damage. | `ShotEvent`: the weapon, the line of the crosshair, the way of the bullet, the number of pellets, the list of hits (the nearest first), and where the bullet stops when it hits nothing. |

```java title="ShotLogPart.java"
ctx.combat().aim(aim -> {
    aim.target().ifPresent(t -> lastChance = t.chance()); // 0 to 1, the chance of the game
});

ctx.combat().shots(new ShotListener() {
    @Override
    public void onShot(ShotEvent shot) {
        for (ShotHit hit : shot.hits()) {
            // hit.id(), hit.kind(), hit.part(), hit.distance(), hit.at(), hit.pellets()
        }
    }

    @Override
    public void onShotEnd(ShotEvent shot) {
        // The game has dealt the damage. Read the health of the targets from the game now.
    }
});
```

- A hit names its target by its kind and the id of the game: `getID()` of a character, `getId()` of a vehicle.
- A hit on a vehicle has the part `NONE`.
- A listener only reads. A listener that throws is a fault: Viewpoint suspends the addon. The other addons still get the
  aim and the shot.

## Sway

A `SwayProvider` adds sway to the crosshair, for example for the breath, a wound or tiredness. Many addons can add sway.

- Viewpoint asks the providers in the order of the player. See [Order](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/order.md).
- Each provider gets the aim with the sway of Viewpoint only. Viewpoint adds the sway of all the providers to it.
- The crosshair and the shot go to the sum, also outside the aim ring.
- All the providers together move the crosshair at most 10 degrees each way.
- Return `Sway.NONE` for no sway. A `null` sway or a number that is not finite is a fault, as a throw is.

```java title="BreathPart.java"
ctx.combat().sway(aim -> {
    double t = System.nanoTime() * 1.0e-9;

    return new Sway(0.0, 0.3 * Math.sin(t * 1.5)); // degrees right, degrees up
});
```

## Decide the result of a shot

A `ShotResolver` decides the list of hits of a shot. This is a **claim**:

- Only one addon at a time can be the resolver. The addon nearer the top of the Active column wins.
- The addon that does not win waits. Its card shows which addon holds the claim.
- Viewpoint releases the claim of an addon that it suspends.

Use a resolver for a change of the rules of a shot, for example a bullet that passes a thin wall. Do not use it only to
read a shot. Use `ShotListener` to read.

```java title="ArmourPart.java"
ResolverClaim claim = ctx.combat().resolve((shot, candidates) -> {
    List<ShotHit> hits = new ArrayList<>();

    for (ShotHit hit : shot.hits()) {
        if (hit.part() != HitPart.SPINE || !wearsArmour(hit.id())) {
            hits.add(hit); // armour on the chest stops the bullet
        }
    }

    return hits;
});
```

- Viewpoint resolves the shot first. Then it gives the shot and its candidates to the resolver. The candidates are what the
  shot can hit, the nearest first.
- Return `shot.hits()` to keep the hits of Viewpoint. Return an empty list for a miss.
- Each hit that you return must name a candidate, or a hit of Viewpoint, by its kind and its id. Viewpoint ignores a hit
  that names nothing of them. Viewpoint puts the hit at the middle of the target.
- The game takes each hit as sure, and deals its damage on the part of the hit.
- A resolver that throws or returns `null` is a fault. The shot then keeps the hits of Viewpoint.
- An addon has one resolver claim open at a time. Close the claim to give it up.

## Reticle

A `ReticleProvider` is a claim. It hides the crosshair dot of Viewpoint and shows a picture of your addon in its place.
Viewpoint draws it. Your addon runs no drawing code.

- Only one addon at a time can hold the reticle. The addon nearer the top of the Active column wins. The others wait.
- The reticle shows where and when the dot shows: in first and third person, while the player looks with the mouse and the
  crosshair is on. It works also without a firearm.
- Viewpoint asks the provider once each frame. The provider returns a `Reticle`: the picture, a scale, a rotation, a tint,
  and whether the aim ring is hidden too. Return `Reticle.NONE` to show nothing. The dot stays hidden while you hold the
  claim.
- The `ReticleState` gives the last aim (while the player aims with the gunplay of Viewpoint), whether the crosshair is on a
  target, whether a fishing cast would not go there, the radius of the aim ring in pixels, the pixels of one degree, and
  the size of the screen.

### Pictures

A picture is a PNG from your package, or a canvas that your addon paints, for a reticle that changes.

```java title="ScopePart.java"
ctx.assets().data().read("reticle.png").then(png -> {
    ReticleImage dot = ctx.combat().image(png); // a PNG in the data folder

    ctx.combat().reticle(state -> new Reticle(
            dot,
            1.0,                          // screen pixels for each pixel of the picture
            0.0,                          // degrees, clockwise
            1.0, state.onTarget() ? 0.2 : 1.0, state.onTarget() ? 0.2 : 1.0, 1.0, // red, green, blue, alpha
            false));                      // true also hides the aim ring
});

ReticleImage canvas = ctx.combat().image(64, 64); // clear at first
canvas.pixels(argb);                              // 64 * 64 pixels, 0xAARRGGBB, from the top left
```

- A picture is at most 512 by 512 pixels. An addon has at most 8 pictures open at a time.
- The pixels of a picture count in `memory.addonDataMiB` until you close it. Viewpoint closes the pictures when the addon
  goes off.
- Set the pixels of a canvas only when they change. Each change goes to the graphics card again.
- A provider that throws, returns `null`, or shows a picture of another addon is a fault. The dot then comes back.

If you want to draw the reticle yourself, use a draw callback at the `crosshair` point. The card of such an addon says
**draws over the whole screen**. See [Draw callbacks](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/draw-callbacks.md).

> **Note**
>
> These types replace the hooks that older addons put on the aim and on the crosshair. Viewpoint refuses a hook on a
> method that has been removed. See [Hooking Viewpoint](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/hooking-viewpoint.md#removed-members).

---

# Model providers

> Choose the model of a world object, or put a model on a bone of a character, from your addon.

A resource pack puts a model on a sprite with a fixed rule. A provider puts a model with code. Use a provider when the
model depends on something that a manifest cannot say.

**Permission:** `models`. The models come from the manifest that your descriptor names with `models=`. See
[Format](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/resource-packs/format.md#models).

```properties
permissions=models
models=models/manifest.txt
```

## ModelProvider: world objects

A `ModelProvider` answers for the sprites that you name. It answers with a `ModelRef`: a model from the manifest of
your addon, placed on the square of the object.

```java
AddonModels models = ctx.models();
ModelRef open = models.model("crate-open", 0, 0, 0, 0, 1);
ModelRef shut = models.model("crate", 0, 0, 0, 0, 1);

models.provide((object, sprite) -> {
    IsoObject crate = (IsoObject) object;

    return crate.getContainer() != null && crate.getContainer().isEmpty() ? open : shut;
}, "furniture_storage_01_5");
```

This provider is not complete. See [When the answer changes](#when-the-answer-changes).

- **Names.** Name the sprites when you register. A name that ends with `*` names all the sprites whose names start with
  the text before it. Viewpoint asks your provider only for the sprites that you name. Every other sprite skips the
  providers.
- **When.** Viewpoint asks when it builds the level of the object, within the ring where it draws the models of the
  packs. It keeps the answer until it builds that level again: when the game changes something on the level, or when
  you call `models.changed(object)`. A change of the items in a container is not one of these changes.
- **Answers.** A `ModelRef` from `models.model(...)`, `ModelRef.NONE` to let the next provider answer, or `ModelRef.ART`
  to show the art of the game.
- **Order.** If several providers name the same sprite, Viewpoint asks them in the order of the player. The first answer
  that is not `ModelRef.NONE` wins. If no provider answers, Viewpoint uses the model of the resource packs. Then it uses
  the art of the game. See [Order](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/order.md).
- **Make your models once.** Call `models.model(...)` before you answer, for example in `enable`. The answer runs on the
  main thread while a level is built, and must not allocate.
- For a model that depends only on whether the object is lit, or that is the same for all the facings of an object, a
  resource pack of version 2 is easier. See [Model states](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/resource-packs/model-states.md).

> **Caution**
>
> These are faults of the addon, and Viewpoint stops the addon for them: a throw, a `null` answer, a `ModelRef` that
> another addon made or that you made yourself, and a model id that your manifest does not have (when Viewpoint first
> draws it). Then it asks the next provider. For an `AttachmentProvider`, a `ModelRef` from `models.model(...)` is also a
> fault: use `models.attachment(...)`.

## When the answer changes

Viewpoint keeps your answer until it builds the level again. The game does not tell Viewpoint when the items of a container
change, so the crate above keeps its old model. You must tell Viewpoint: call `models.changed(object)` when your answer
changes. To know when it changes, use a [hook](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/managed-patching.md).

```properties
permissions=models,hooks
models=models/manifest.txt
hooks.targets=zombie.inventory.ItemContainer
```

```java title="CrateHooks.java"
public final class CrateHooks {
    private static final String CRATE = "furniture_storage_01_5";
    private static AddonModels models;

    private CrateHooks() {}

    /** Call this in {@code enable} with {@code ctx.models()}. */
    static void start(AddonModels addonModels) {
        models = addonModels;
    }

    @Hook.After(target = "zombie.inventory.ItemContainer", method = "AddItem",
            descriptor = "(Lzombie/inventory/InventoryItem;)Lzombie/inventory/InventoryItem;")
    public static void added(ItemContainer container, InventoryItem item, InventoryItem result) {
        if (container.getItems().size() == 1) {
            changed(container);
        }
    }

    @Hook.After(target = "zombie.inventory.ItemContainer", method = "Remove",
            descriptor = "(Lzombie/inventory/InventoryItem;)V")
    public static void removed(ItemContainer container, InventoryItem item) {
        if (container.isEmpty()) {
            changed(container);
        }
    }

    @Hook.After(target = "zombie.inventory.ItemContainer", method = "DoRemoveItem",
            descriptor = "(Lzombie/inventory/InventoryItem;)V")
    public static void doRemoved(ItemContainer container, InventoryItem item) {
        if (container.isEmpty()) {
            changed(container);
        }
    }

    private static void changed(ItemContainer container) {
        IsoObject crate = container.getParent();

        if (crate != null && crate.getSprite() != null && CRATE.equals(crate.getSprite().getName())) {
            models.changed(crate);
        }
    }
}
```

- **Call `changed` only when the answer changes.** Each call builds the level of the object again. These handlers call it
  only when a crate becomes empty, or stops being empty, and only for the sprite of your provider. The hooks run for
  each container of the game, also for the inventory of the player.
- **What these hooks see.** When the player moves an item, the game calls these three methods. The game has other methods
  that change a container, for example `AddItem(String)` and `removeAllItems()`. To follow them, hook them too. A change
  that you do not hook shows when the game next builds the level.
- **The hooks wait for a safe point.** Until then, nothing calls `changed`. See
  [When hooks install](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/managed-patching.md#when-hooks-install).

## AttachmentProvider: characters

An `AttachmentProvider` puts a model on a bone of a character that Viewpoint draws: a hat, a pack, a lamp on a belt.

```java
AddonModels models = ctx.models();
ModelRef hat = models.attachment("cowboy-hat", "Bip01_Head", 0, 0.1f, 0, 0, 90, 0, 1);

models.attach(character -> ((IsoGameCharacter) character).isZombie() ? hat : ModelRef.NONE);
```

- **The attachment.** `models.attachment(id, bone, x, y, z, turnX, turnY, turnZ, scale)` makes a model of your manifest
  on a bone of the game's skeleton, for example `Bip01_Head`, `Bip01_Spine1` or `Bip01_R_Hand`. The model keeps the axes
  of its OBJ file, put on the axes of the bone. Viewpoint turns it about the x, then the y, then the z axis of the bone
  by the degrees that you give, scales it, then moves it by the offset. The units are those of the resource packs: one
  is the side of a square. On a character that does not have the bone, the model is not drawn.
- **Answers.** A `ModelRef` from `models.attachment(...)`, or `ModelRef.NONE` for no attachment. `ModelRef.ART` is the
  same as `ModelRef.NONE`.
- **When.** Viewpoint asks each provider once for each character that it draws, in each frame. A crowd asks many times
  each frame: keep the answer cheap, and make your attachments before you answer, for example in `enable`.
- **Many on one bone.** Viewpoint draws every answer. Many providers, of your addon or of other addons, can put models
  on the same bone. To put two models on a character, add two providers.
- The model follows the bone in all the poses of the character, also in a crowd far away. On the player's own head in
  first person, it only casts a shadow, as a hat of the game does.
- The model comes from the manifest of your addon. It counts in `memory.packMiB`. See
  [Assets & budgets](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/performance/assets-and-budgets.md).
- An attachment shows all its parts. The `[lit]` and `[!lit]` tags of [Model states](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/resource-packs/model-states.md) are
  for world objects only, and an attachment does not glow.

## Cost

Both types are on a hot path of the game. Viewpoint measures them and shows the time on the **Performance** tab.

- Keep your answers fast. A slow `ModelProvider` makes the levels slower to build. A slow `AttachmentProvider`
  makes each frame slower.
- Each attachment is one more model that Viewpoint draws, with its shadow.
- With no provider, the providers add no cost.

> **Tip**
>
> Use `ModelProvider` only for sprites that need code. Use a resource pack for the others. The pack path has no code, and
> the label stays simple.

---

# Shader values

> Give numbers from your addon to shader code, as uniforms with the name of your addon in them.

A shader value is a number that your addon sets on the main thread. Viewpoint gives it to shader code as a uniform. Use
it to let a Shaderpack, a snippet or a `Gpu` program react to your addon, for example to the lean of a camera.

**Permission:** `shaders`.

```properties
permissions=shaders
```

## Declare and set

Your addon declares each value with a name and a kind. Then it sets the value on the main thread. The kinds
(`ValueKind`) are `FLOAT`, `VEC2`, `VEC3`, `VEC4`, `INT` and `MAT4`.

- Declare each value when the addon starts. Set it on the main thread, as often as you want. Viewpoint copies the values
  into the frame once each frame, if one changed.
- `set` takes as many numbers as the kind holds: 1 for `FLOAT` and `INT`, 2 to 4 for the vectors, 16 by columns for
  `MAT4`.
- A pulse records the moment of an event. Shader code reads a `vec2`: the seconds since the last event, and its
  strength from 0 to 1. Before the first event, the seconds are 1,000,000.
- An addon has 32 values and pulses at most.

```java title="LeanPart.java"
ShaderValues values = ctx.shaders().values();
ShaderValue angle = values.declare("angle", ValueKind.FLOAT);
ShaderPulse step = values.pulse("step");

// Later, on the main thread:
angle.set(leanDegrees);
step.fire(0.6f);
```

## Read it in GLSL

The name of the uniform is `uAddon_<encoded id>_<name>`. The encoded id writes `.` and `-` as `_`.

```glsl
uniform float uAddon_example_lean_angle;
```

For the addon `example.lean` and the value `angle`, this is the name above. Viewpoint sets the value on each Viewpoint
program that declares the uniform. This includes:

- the passes of a Shaderpack. See [Passes & inputs](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/shaderpacks/passes-and-inputs.md#values-of-addons);
- the snippets of addons. See [Shader snippets](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/shader-snippets.md);
- the programs that you make with `Gpu`. See [Draw callbacks](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/draw-callbacks.md);
- the programs of an Iris pack. Viewpoint binds the values by name for each program that declares them.

A program that does not declare the uniform gets nothing. A declared value that you have not set is 0. When your addon
goes off, its values are 0 again.

## Rules

- A value name has letters and digits only, and it starts with a letter. Write it in camelCase, for example `leanAngle`.
  Viewpoint refuses any other name when you declare the value. Thus a name has one reading in GLSL.
- Only your addon sets the values of your addon.
- No addon code runs on the render thread to set a value. The values come in the snapshot of the frame.

> **Note**
>
> The game gives events of the fight itself, for example a shot. You do not have to pulse them. See
> [Passes & inputs](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/shaderpacks/passes-and-inputs.md#event-values).

---

# Managed patching

> Declare hooks into game methods. Viewpoint installs them at safe points, runs them in the player's order and lists them.

A **hook** connects a **handler** to a game method. A handler is a static method of yours. Viewpoint runs it when the
game method starts or ends. You declare the hook. Viewpoint installs it.

Viewpoint reads your hooks from the jar before it shows the consent dialog. It runs the hooks of all active addons in
the player's order. The player can see each active hook and veto it.

**Permission:** `hooks`, with each hooked class in `hooks.targets`. You can hook game methods and the listed methods of Viewpoint. See [Hooking Viewpoint](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/hooking-viewpoint.md). You cannot hook a class of another addon.

```properties
permissions=hooks
hooks.targets=zombie.characters.IsoPlayer
```

## Declare a hook

```java title="HookPart.java"
public final class HookPart {
    @Hook.After(target = "zombie.characters.IsoPlayer", method = "update", descriptor = "()V")
    public static void afterUpdate(HookCall call) {
        IsoPlayer player = (IsoPlayer) call.self();
        // observe the player once a tick
    }
}
```

- `@Hook.Before` runs before the game method. `@Hook.After` runs after it.
- Put the annotation on a `public static` method.
- The handler has one parameter, a `HookCall`, or it is a [typed handler](#typed-handlers) and takes the values of the call.
- You do not register the handler. Viewpoint finds the annotations when it reads the jar.

| Attribute | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `target` | The binary name of the class. It must be in `hooks.targets`. |
| `method` | The name of the method. |
| `descriptor` | The JVM descriptor of the method, for example `()V` or `(I)Z`. It selects the overload. |
| `kind` | What the handler can do: `OBSERVE` (the default), `ARGS`, `RETURN` or `SKIP`. |
| `thread` | `MAIN` (the default), `ANY` or `RENDER`. See [Threads](#threads). |

### Kinds

Each kind can do all that the kinds before it can do.

| Kind | The handler can |
| --- | --- |
| `OBSERVE` | Read the call: `self()`, `arg(i)`. In an `After`, also `returned()` and `thrown()`. |
| `ARGS` | Also change an argument before the game method runs: `setArg(i, value)`. |
| `RETURN` | Also replace the return value: `setReturn(value)`. |
| `SKIP` | Also stop the game method: `skip()`. A `Before` that calls `setReturn` also skips the method. |

If a handler does more than its kind lets it do, it gets an `IllegalStateException`, and Viewpoint suspends the addon.
The player gives consent to the kind. A stronger kind in an update needs consent again.

Use the weakest kind that does the work.

### Typed handlers

A handler with a `HookCall` boxes every argument. This costs about 50 nanoseconds a call. For a method that the game calls
very often, write a **typed handler**. It takes the values of the call as typed parameters, and it has no `HookCall`.
Viewpoint boxes nothing for it, and it makes no call record.

```java
@Hook.After(target = "zombie.characters.IsoPlayer", method = "update", descriptor = "()V")
public static void afterUpdate(IsoPlayer player) {
    // runs for each call, with the object that the method ran on
}
```

The parameters of a typed handler are these, in this order:

1. Optional: the object that the method runs on, for an instance method. It has the type of the class.
2. The parameters of the method, with their types.
3. Optional, in an `After` only: the result of the method, when it gives one.

A typed handler returns nothing, and it is a hook of kind `OBSERVE`: it reads the call and cannot change it. If a
handler must change an argument or the result, or skip the method, it takes a `HookCall`. A typed `After` runs when the
method returns. It does not run when the method throws. A typed handler with `thread = ANY` cannot take the object.

A parameter has the type that the method has. If the method's type is a class of Viewpoint, which your jar cannot name,
the parameter is `Object`. Viewpoint refuses a handler whose parameters do not fit, and the card tells why. A typed
handler on a method that the game calls more than 1,000 times each frame does not make a **costly hook**. A handler with
a `HookCall` there does.

A typed `After` sees the parameters as the method leaves them. If the method assigns to a parameter, the handler sees
the new value. A handler with a `HookCall` sees the values that the method was called with.

A typed handler must not call its own method, directly or through other code. It has no guard against a recursion: the
call ends in a `StackOverflowError`, and Viewpoint suspends the addon.

Two typed handlers of one method can be of two addons. If one handler on the method takes a `HookCall`, Viewpoint calls
the typed ones through the boxed path, and the method pays the cost of it again.

### `HookCall`

| Member | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `self()` | The object of the call. `null` for a static method. |
| `arg(i)`, `argCount()` | The arguments, boxed. |
| `returned()` | In an `After`: the return value, boxed, or `null`. |
| `thrown()` | In an `After`: the exception from the method, or `null`. Read only. |
| `setArg(i, v)`, `setReturn(v)`, `skip()` | Changes, as the kind lets you. |
| `state()`, `setState(o)` | A value that your `Before` keeps for your `After` of the same call. Only your handler sees it. |

`setArg` and `setReturn` check the type of the value against the method descriptor:

- For a primitive, give its exact wrapper type. Do not give `null`.
- For a reference, give an instance of the declared class.

If the type is not correct, your handler gets an `IllegalArgumentException`, and Viewpoint suspends the addon. The
incorrect value does not go to the game.

A hook with `thread = ANY` or `thread = RENDER` is installed where its thread fits the member (see [Threads](#threads)).
Viewpoint refuses one that does not fit when it reads the jar, so the player does not see a consent dialog for it.

A value that is an object of your own addon is not accepted either: the game would then keep your code, and your addon
could not unload. Viewpoint looks at the value, and at the elements of an array, a list, a set or a map one level inside
it. It does not look deeper, and it does not look inside a wrapper that is not a container (a `Thread`, a
`FutureTask`, an `Optional`). Do not hide an object of your addon in a wrapper to give it to the game: a hook that does
this is your bug, and Viewpoint cannot promise to find it.

## When the game calls a hooked method

1. **Start.** The `Before` handlers run, from the top of the Active column to the bottom.
2. If a handler **skips or replaces** the call, the handlers below it are *pre-empted*. Their `Before` and `After` do
   not run. The card counts them.
3. The game method runs, if no handler skipped it.
4. **End.** The `After` handlers run from bottom to top. The pre-empted handlers do not run.

If the game method **throws an exception**, the `After` handlers run, and `thrown()` gives the exception. They cannot
stop or replace the exception. Viewpoint ignores their changes to the return value. The exception goes on, with no
change.

Viewpoint keeps a copy of the handler list from the start of the call. A veto or a new order during the call does not
change which `After` handlers run for that call.

## Threads

Hooks run on the main thread by default. If a different thread calls the hooked method, **your handler does not run**.
The card counts *skipped off-thread*.

With `thread = ANY`, your handler runs on the thread that calls the method. Viewpoint accepts `thread = ANY` only when
both of these are true:

- Your handler does not call `self()`. If it does, `self()` throws an `IllegalStateException`, and Viewpoint suspends
  the addon. Your handler must not keep the `HookCall` or pass it to a lambda.
- Each parameter and the return type is a primitive, a boxed primitive or `String`.

A `thread = ANY` hook makes the label **Amber**. Your handler must not use game objects.

With `thread = RENDER`, your handler runs on the render thread. Use it only for a method of Viewpoint that the
[internals list](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/reference/viewpoint-internals.md) marks as a render method. A `RENDER` handler can read and set the
arguments and the return value. It cannot use `Gpu` or OpenGL: Viewpoint refuses the jar when the handler's code, or a
method that it calls, can reach either. If the method is called on another thread, Viewpoint does not run the handler,
and the card counts the call. A `RENDER` hook makes the label Red.

## When a handler fails

| Event | Result |
| --- | --- |
| A `Throwable` goes out of a handler | Viewpoint suspends the addon for the session. `console.txt` gets `[Viewpoint] addon <id> suspended: <hook> threw ...` and the stack trace. The player switches the addon on again to try again. |
| Your handler calls a hooked method | Viewpoint does not run your handlers again during your handler. |
| A hook does not install | The addon is **Failed**. The card gives the cause. The game method does not change. |

## Cost

Viewpoint measures the time of your handlers, for each addon and each hook. The **Performance** tab of the card shows the
values. Viewpoint's profiler shows them under the group `ADDONS`.

| Mark | When | On the card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Slow hook** | One handler call takes more than 1 ms, or the handlers take more than 2 ms each frame for 60 frames | Flag |
| **Costly hook** | The game calls the method more than 1,000 times each frame, from any thread, and the handler is not typed | Flag |

Viewpoint finds these marks while the addon runs. Thus they are flags on the card, and they do not change the label that
the player sees before consent. A later release can add them to the label.

An addon with no active hooks adds no cost to the game.

A handler call with a `HookCall` costs about 50 nanoseconds. A method that the game calls 1,000 times each frame then adds
about 0.05 ms to each frame. Use a **costly hook** only if no other method gives you the event, and then write a typed
handler. A `RENDER` hook is also counted in the time of the render thread.

## When hooks install

Viewpoint installs and removes hooks only at **safe points** (see
[Lifecycle & threads](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/lifecycle-and-threads.md#safe-points)). Until the next safe point, the state is *Active:
hooks pending*. Use `ctx.hooksLive()` or `ctx.onHooksLive(Runnable)` to know when your hooks are installed.

## The hook list

Viewpoint shows each active hook in four places:

- on the card, under **Hooks**, with a veto for each hook;
- in `console.txt`, for example `[Viewpoint] addon example.lean hook zombie.characters.IsoPlayer.update()V after active`
  (or `vetoed`);
- in the crash report;
- in Viewpoint's health line.

The player can veto a hook in **Info**, **Hooks**. The veto stops the handler at once, and Viewpoint keeps it for the
next start. The advice stays on the game's class until the next change of the hooks. A method whose hooks are all vetoed costs
the game a check and no more. When the
player switches an addon off, its handlers stop at once.

## What hooks cost

A hook costs nothing while no addon has one: Viewpoint does no work for hooks in a frame then. For an addon with hooks,
the profiler shows the time that the addon takes on the main thread each frame as `addon.<id>.mainMs` (its handlers and
its Lua exports), the time of its `ANY` handlers on other threads as `addon.<id>.workerMs`, and the time of Viewpoint's
own work for hooks in the group **Addons**. The time on other threads is sampled: one call in 16 on a site that the game
calls often. A method that is called from another thread than a `MAIN` hook expects costs one counter, and nothing
else. The card counts those calls under *skipped off-thread*, for each hook
of the method.

> **Note**
>
> You can keep your ZombieBuddy `@Patch` classes. Viewpoint reads them in an addon jar. See
> [Migrating from ZombieBuddy](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/migrating-from-zombiebuddy.md).

---

# Hooking Viewpoint

> Hook the methods of Viewpoint that are on the internals list. Which threads, which levels, and what happens when a member is removed.

> **This release**
>
> In this release you can hook a listed member of Viewpoint with a `MAIN` hook (a member that runs on the main thread) or
> with an `ANY` hook (a member that other threads call, with values only). A `RENDER` hook, for a member that runs on the
> render thread, comes with the renderer API; Viewpoint refuses it now.

An addon can hook some methods of Viewpoint itself, and read some of its members. This is for the cases where
`viewpoint.api` does not have what you need. Look at `viewpoint.api` first.

Viewpoint lets you use only the members on the [internals list](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/reference/viewpoint-internals.md). It does not load a jar
that uses another member of Viewpoint.

## Use, hook and reflect

The list gives three ways to reach a member. Each has a rule.

| Way | Rule | Level |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Hook** | You can hook a listed method of any access: public, protected, package or private. | The grade of the list |
| **Use** | You can call a method or read a field only when the member and its class are both public. | The grade of the list |
| **Reflect** | You can find a listed member by reflection. | Always Red |

- Viewpoint does not make code public for addons. A private method can be hooked, but not called.
- A write to a field of Viewpoint is refused. The message names the API that replaces the write, for example camera
  layers.
- A member can be **hook only**. You can hook it, but you cannot call it. The list says so.
- Every member has a grade: Amber or Red. An addon that uses or hooks a member is never Normal.
- The code that runs the hooks is never listed, so you cannot hook it. That is the classes `AddonHooks`, `AddonTrampoline`
  and `SiteId`, and the classes that Viewpoint makes for a typed hook while it runs.

## Declare the hook

Declare a hook on a Viewpoint method as you declare one on a game method. See
[Managed patching](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/managed-patching.md). The target is the class on the internals list. The method name and
the descriptor are the ones that the list gives for the member. Put the class in `hooks.targets`, as for a game class.
The consent dialog and the update list each hooked member of Viewpoint.

The kinds, `HookCall` and the order of handlers are the same as for game methods.

**Types.** Your jar cannot name a class of Viewpoint that is not public and listed. Thus a handler gets a Viewpoint object
as `Object`, and `call.self()` gives an `Object`. A typed handler takes only primitives, types of `viewpoint.api` and
game types. A Viewpoint object that passes through it arrives boxed.

## Threads

Each member on the list has a thread. The thread tells you which hook you can use.

| The list says | You can use |
| --- | --- |
| `main` | A `thread = MAIN` hook. |
| `render` | Only a `thread = RENDER` hook. Viewpoint refuses a `MAIN` hook on this member when it reads the jar. |
| `any` | A hook with `thread = MAIN`. It does not run when another thread calls the member, and the card counts that call as *skipped off-thread*. Or a hook with `thread = ANY`, on a member whose parameters and result are values only. |
| `worker` | Only a hook with `thread = ANY`. The handler takes values only. Viewpoint refuses a `MAIN` hook on this member when it reads the jar. |

A `RENDER` hook runs on the render thread. It can read and set the arguments and the return value. It cannot draw. It
cannot use `Gpu` or OpenGL. Viewpoint refuses a jar that does. A hook on a `render` member is Red.

The card lists the hooks on members of Viewpoint apart from the hooks on the game, and `console.txt` ends their line with
"(a member of Viewpoint)".

If Viewpoint calls the method on another thread than the hook expects, your handler does not run. The card counts the
call as *skipped off-thread*.

## Hot members

Some members run more than 1,000 times each frame. A hook on them is a **costly hook**, and the label is Amber. A typed
handler is much cheaper than a boxed one. See [Managed patching](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/managed-patching.md#typed-handlers).

## Replacements

For some of the most hooked members, `viewpoint.api` has a better way. Use it when you can.

| Member | Replacement |
| --- | --- |
| `ModelCapture.capture`, to put a model on a bone | `AttachmentProvider`. See [Model providers](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/model-providers.md). |
| `PackGather.object` | `ModelProvider`. See [Model providers](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/model-providers.md). |
| `Shaders.read` | Shader snippets, or a Shaderpack. See [Shader snippets](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/shader-snippets.md) and [Shaderpack format](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/shaderpacks/format.md). |
| `Eye.place` | Camera layers. See [Camera layers](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/camera-layers.md). |

`AttachmentProvider` adds a model to a bone. It does not move a bone. This release has no API that changes the pose of a
character. A hook on `ModelCapture.capture` is the only way that Viewpoint lists, and its level is Red. An API for this is
planned for API 1.1.

## Removed members

Viewpoint changes in each release. A member that Viewpoint removes is marked **gone** in the list, with the release and
the replacement.

- An addon that uses or hooks a gone member shows **Needs an update**. The card says: "uses \<member\>, removed in
  \<release\>; use \<replacement\>", or "...; nothing replaces it". The addon does not start. It starts again when its
  author makes a new version that does not use the member.
- Some members are only **deprecated**. The addon works. The card shows the replacement and the Amber reason **uses
  deprecated internals**.
- A member whose descriptor changes is a gone member plus a new member.

Examples of members that are gone: `FP.snapshot` (use `ViewListener.onFrame`) and `SceneDrawer.drawCrosshair` (use
`ReticleProvider`, or the `crosshair` draw point). The page [Internals changes](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/reference/internals-changes.md) lists the
changes of each release.

> **Caution**
>
> A listed member has no promise of stability. Test your addon after each Viewpoint release. A new member in an update
> needs the consent of the player again.

## Hooks of other addons

Viewpoint refuses a hook on a class of another addon. If you need an extension point, ask the author to publish a service.
See [Services](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/services.md).

---

# Migrating from ZombieBuddy

> Change a ZombieBuddy mod into an addon. Keep its @Patch classes, or write hooks.

A mod that loads Java through ZombieBuddy (`javaJarFile` in `mod.info`) is **Unmanaged**. Viewpoint cannot order it,
switch it off, check it, or show its hooks. When you change the mod into an addon, the player gets these controls. You
get a stable API in place of reflection into Viewpoint.

## What changes

| | ZombieBuddy mod (Unmanaged) | Addon |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Loaded by | ZombieBuddy, when the game starts | Viewpoint, when the player switches it on |
| Declared by | `javaJarFile` in `mod.info` | `jar=` in `addon.properties` |
| Player control | None in Viewpoint | Order, on and off, veto of each hook, no restart |
| Checked | No | Yes, with a label |
| Patches | `@Patch` classes, for the full session | `@Hook` handlers, or `@Patch` classes, installed at safe points |
| Access to Viewpoint | Reflection into `viewpoint.*` | `viewpoint.api`, and the members in the Viewpoint internals list |
| Lua | `@Exposer` | Exports. Viewpoint reads your `@Exposer.LuaClass` classes as exports, with the name as a requested global. |
| Files and network | All that Java can do | `AddonFiles` and `AddonDownloads` |

## Two methods

### 1. Keep your `@Patch` classes

Viewpoint reads ZombieBuddy `@Patch` classes in an addon jar. It runs them as hooks, so the player can order, veto and
see them. This is the fastest method. Viewpoint accepts only part of the `@Patch` features.

| ZombieBuddy | Becomes |
| --- | --- |
| `@Patch(className, methodName)` on the class | The target and the method of the hook. The class must be in `hooks.targets`. |
| `@Patch.OnEnter` | A `Before` hook |
| `@Patch.OnEnter(skipOn = true)` | A `Before` hook of kind `SKIP` |
| `@Patch.OnExit` | An `After` hook. It runs after a normal return. `onThrowable = Throwable.class` runs it after a throw also. |
| `@Patch.This`, `@Patch.Argument`, `@Patch.AllArguments`, `@Patch.Return` | `self()`, `arg(i)`, the arguments, `returned()` |
| `@Patch.Argument(readOnly = false)` and `@Patch.AllArguments(readOnly = false)`, in an `OnEnter` | A write to the parameter changes the argument that the method gets. The hook then has kind `ARGS`. |
| `@Patch.Return(readOnly = false)`, in an `OnExit` | A write to the parameter replaces the result of the method. The hook then has kind `RETURN`. |
| `@Patch.Local("name")` | A value that the `OnEnter` writes and the `OnExit` of the same patch reads, for the same call. |

Overloads match as in ZombieBuddy. If a patch method has no arguments, `strictMatch` controls the match: all overloads,
or only the overloads with no arguments. Viewpoint finds the overloads when the addon starts, in the game as it is, and
shows one hook for each. If the patch matches no overload, the addon does not start, and the card says why.

**Not accepted.** Viewpoint cannot run these as hooks:

- `isAdvice = false` (ByteBuddy's `MethodDelegation`);
- a class or a method name that is a pattern (`*`, or a regular expression between `/`): name one class and one method,
  and put the class in `hooks.targets`;
- a constructor (`<init>`);
- a write to `@This` (Viewpoint cannot change the object that a method runs on), and a write to an argument in an
  `OnExit` (the method has run);
- an `OnExit` with `suppress`, or with an `onThrowable` other than `Throwable.class`;
- an `OnEnter(skipOn = true)` that does not return a `boolean`;
- `@SuperCall` and `@SuperMethod`;
- writes to `@Thrown`;
- `warmUp` and `IKnowWhatIAmDoing`;
- ByteBuddy annotations used directly (`FieldValue`, `Origin`, `StubValue`).

A mod that needs one of these must stay a ZombieBuddy mod.

**Writes.** A write to a parameter takes effect when the advice returns, as in ZombieBuddy. If the advice writes an
argument and then reads it through `@AllArguments`, it sees the old value. A write counts when the advice puts another
object in the parameter, also one that equals the first (a copy of a list). If the call refuses one of the values that the
advice wrote (a value of a wrong type), Viewpoint puts back all the arguments, suspends the addon, and the method runs
with the arguments it was called with.

**Threads.** ZombieBuddy runs a patch on the thread that calls the method. Viewpoint does the same for a patch that is
fit for it: one that takes values only (`@Argument`, `@Return`, primitives and `String`), and not the object (`@This`) or
`@AllArguments`. It runs on any thread, as a hook with `thread = ANY` does, and the label is Amber: the same patch that you ran as a ZombieBuddy mod
shows an Amber line in an addon, and adding `@This` makes the hook run on the main thread only and the label Normal. A patch that reads
`@This` runs on the **main thread only**: where another thread calls the method, the patch does not run, and the card
counts the call as *skipped off-thread*. Check the methods that you patch: a chunk, a light or a sound accessor is often
called by workers.

**Checked when the addon starts.** Viewpoint reads the game and checks each advice against each overload that the patch
matches. If an advice asks for an argument that an overload does not have, or for a result of the wrong type or from a
method that gives none, or for an object of another class, the addon does not start, and the card names the parameter and
the overload. ZombieBuddy reports these as errors when it applies the patch. An advice that reads the result with an
`Object` parameter (`@Patch.Return Object result`) is not refused where an overload gives no result: as under ZombieBuddy, it
gets `null`. A `@Patch.Return` that writes, or one of a primitive type, is refused there.

A patch with no parameter at all, and not `strictMatch`, is applied to every overload of the method. The consent shows it
as one hook on any thread; the card shows each overload, and an overload that takes an object runs on the main thread only.

**A bridge method.** The compiler makes a bridge method for a covariant return. ZombieBuddy patches it as well as the
real method, so a patch can run twice for one call. Viewpoint leaves synthetic methods alone, and the patch runs once.
Count calls with this in mind.

**The pilot.** `pilotaddon` patches `IsoPlayer.update`, which the main thread calls. If a player installs both the
ZombieBuddy mod and the addon of the pilot, the patch runs twice: once from each.

### 2. Write `@Hook` handlers

Write each patch again as a `@Hook.Before` or `@Hook.After` method with a `HookCall` parameter. The change is small. The
kind of each hook is then clear, and the player sees what it can do. See [Managed patching](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/managed-patching.md).

```java title="Before: ZombieBuddy"
@Patch(className = "zombie.characters.IsoPlayer", methodName = "update")
public final class UpdatePatch {
    @Patch.OnExit
    public static void exit(@Patch.This IsoPlayer self) {
        Counter.tick(self);
    }
}
```

```java title="After: addon"
public final class UpdateHook {
    @Hook.After(target = "zombie.characters.IsoPlayer", method = "update", descriptor = "()V")
    public static void exit(HookCall call) {
        Counter.tick((IsoPlayer) call.self());
    }
}
```

## Your `@Exposer.LuaClass` classes

Viewpoint reads these classes as [Lua exports](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/lua-exports.md), so the Lua of your mod can keep its names. The addon
needs the `lua` permission.

| In ZombieBuddy | In an addon |
| --- | --- |
| The public static methods of the class, and of its superclasses | The public static methods that your jar declares, its superclasses in the jar included. `@HiddenFromLua` keeps a method out. |
| `name = "A.B"` | The table `A` with `B` in it. Lua finds the class also as `Viewpoint.Addons["<id>"].B`. |
| A blank `name` | The simple name of the class, at the top level. |
| The global exists at once | The global exists only if `lua.globals` lists it (for `A.B`, list `A`). Without it, only `Viewpoint.Addons["<id>"]` works, and `console.txt` says so. |
| Public static fields | **Not exported.** Write a static method that returns the value. |
| Public constructors (`X.new`) | **Not exported.** Write a static method that makes the object, or a handle. |
| Instance methods | **Not exported.** Lua can call them only on an object it already has. |
| Overloads | **Refused.** Name each method differently, with `@LuaExport(name = "...")` if you need to. |
| Any argument that Kahlua can convert | A closed set of types. See [The types](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/lua-exports.md#the-types). |

If a class has `@LuaExport` as well as `@Exposer.LuaClass`, Viewpoint reads it through `@LuaExport` only. The other
public static methods of the class are not exports, and its `@Exposer.LuaClass` name is not asked for as a global.
Viewpoint tells you this in `console.txt` (and on the card, when the card shows it): remove one of the two
annotations.

## What to use in place of what

Some code that works in a ZombieBuddy mod has a better place in an addon.

| In your ZombieBuddy mod | In an addon |
| --- | --- |
| `@Exposer` classes, so that Lua calls your Java | Exports with `@LuaExport`. Your `@Exposer.LuaClass` classes also work, in part (see above): the name is a *requested* global, and Viewpoint refuses it if another mod has it. Exports install within the start limit. See [Lua exports](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/lua-exports.md). |
| A patch on `Shaders.read` that changes library GLSL | A shader snippet, or a Shaderpack. See [Shader snippets](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/shader-snippets.md) and [Shaderpack format](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/shaderpacks/format.md). |
| Reflection to read the view or the camera | `ViewState` on the main thread, and `FrameView` in a draw callback. See [View state](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/view-state.md). |
| Writes to the look, the eye, the field of view or the view mode | Camera layers and claims. See [Camera layers](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/camera-layers.md). |
| Hooks or reflection on the aim, the shot and the crosshair | `AimListener`, `ShotListener`, `ShotResolver` and `ReticleProvider`. See [Aim & shots](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/aim-and-shots.md). |
| A patch on the choice of the model of an object or a character | `ModelProvider` and `AttachmentProvider`. See [Model providers](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/model-providers.md). |
| Direct OpenGL calls | The `Gpu` object in a draw callback. See [Draw callbacks](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/draw-callbacks.md) (planned). |
| A hook on another mod's classes | A service of that mod. See [Services](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/services.md). |
| An installer jar that copies a shader pack | A Shaderpack. See [Migrating from Java](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/shaderpacks/migrating-from-java.md). |

If `viewpoint.api` has no replacement for a member that you use, you can hook or call some members of Viewpoint itself.
See [Hooking Viewpoint](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/hooking-viewpoint.md).

## The procedure

1. Remove `javaJarFile` from `mod.info`. Keep `require=Viewpoint`. If `javaJarFile` stays, ZombieBuddy loads the jar.
2. Add `addon.properties`, with `jar=` and `entry=`. The `entry` class must implement `Addon`.
3. Add `permissions`. Add `hooks.targets`, `files.quotaMiB` and `downloads.hosts` as necessary.
4. Replace reflection into `viewpoint.*` with `viewpoint.api`. If the API does not have what you need, use or hook a
   member from the [Viewpoint internals list](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/reference/viewpoint-internals.md). This gives an Amber or Red label.
5. Replace `java.io.File` with `AddonFiles`.
6. Replace `java.net` with `AddonDownloads`.
7. Remove all use of ZombieBuddy and ByteBuddy classes. Viewpoint does not load a jar that uses them.
8. Move the start-up code of your `Main` into `enable`. Viewpoint runs `enable` when the player switches the addon on.
9. Undo that work in `disable`, or get it as a `Registration`.
10. Switch the addon on, and read its label. Remove the items that the label names, if you can.
11. In your changelog, tell the player why you need the items that stay.

If you also keep a ZombieBuddy build of the mod, give the two builds different mod ids.

## Your label

Some code that works in a ZombieBuddy mod makes the label Amber or Red in an addon. Some code stops the jar from
loading, for example your own classes in a `zombie.*` package. See [Labels](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/trust/labels.md) for what to use.

> **The ZombieBuddy policy applies**
>
> If the ZombieBuddy policy is `deny-new`, no addon with Java can start. See
> [ZombieBuddy policy & signatures](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/trust/relation-to-zombiebuddy.md).

---

# Hookable targets & refusals

> The methods that an addon can hook, and the targets that Viewpoint refuses before the player sees a dialog.

You must declare the target class of each hook in the descriptor. The target must also be a class that Viewpoint lets
you hook. Viewpoint checks both when it reads the jar. Thus the player never sees a consent dialog for a hook that
cannot install.

## Declare the targets

Put the classes in `hooks.targets`, with commas between them:

```properties
permissions=hooks
hooks.targets=zombie.characters.IsoPlayer,zombie.iso.IsoGridSquare
```

Viewpoint refuses each `@Hook` whose `target` is not in this list. The list takes the classes of Viewpoint that are on
the [internals list](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/reference/viewpoint-internals.md), as it takes game classes. A new class in the list needs the
player's consent again. For a class of Viewpoint, each new hooked member needs it also. See [Updates & changelogs](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/trust/updates-and-changelogs.md).

## Refused targets

| Target | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| Viewpoint's classes and members that are not in the [Viewpoint internals list](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/reference/viewpoint-internals.md) | Use `viewpoint.api`, or a member from the list. A hook on a listed member gives an Amber or Red label. See [Hooking Viewpoint](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/hooking-viewpoint.md). |
| Classes of another addon | Hooks on the code of another author cannot be ordered or checked. Ask the author to publish a [service](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/services.md). |
| Java's classes | These are not the game's classes. |
| ZombieBuddy and ByteBuddy | These load and patch the game. |
| Game code that reads files or opens network connections, as far as Viewpoint can read it | Viewpoint does not let addons change it. |
| LWJGL, Kahlua and the other libraries in the game jar | These are not the game's code. They reach memory, native code and the Lua VM. |
| Constructors and static initialisers (`<init>`, `<clinit>`) | The object does not exist yet when the hook runs. |

Viewpoint decides some things only when it installs the hook, because it has to read the game for them: a method that is
not in this build, that is abstract or native, that is static when a typed handler takes the object, or that gives no
result when a typed handler takes the result. For a ZombieBuddy patch it also decides the overloads, and whether the advice
