vertex or fragment stage. You do not have to do anything for them. Declare each colour output of a fragment stage with its location, `layout(location = N)`.

A few points are inside a shader. The library marks them with comments:

```glsl
// @viewpoint point surface
```

If you replace a library file that has a marker, keep the marker line in the same place in your file. If you drop a
marker, the snippets of that point do not run in your pack. A message on the Addons page says "the shaderpack X has no
point Y". See [Shader snippets](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/shader-snippets.md).

## Made for a version

Set `library=` in your descriptor to the Viewpoint version that you made your pack for. Some library files that your
pack replaces can change after that version. Then the card says "made for \<version\>: N of the files it replaces have
changed since". This is a notice for the player. It does not stop the pack.

This notice is planned. It can come after API 1.0.

---

# Migrating from Java

> Change a mod that copies a shader pack into the player's folder into a Shaderpack that Viewpoint manages.

Some mods have a jar with one job: it copies a shader pack into `Zomboid/viewpoint-shaderpacks`. These mods load their
Java through ZombieBuddy. Viewpoint shows them as **Unmanaged**. A Shaderpack does the same job with no Java. The player
can then switch it off, see its label, and update it with the mod.

## What changes

| | Installer jar | Shaderpack |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Where the pack is | Copied into the player's folder | In the mod, in `media/viewpoint/shaderpacks/<id>/` |
| Java | A jar that ZombieBuddy loads | None |
| Player control | None | Activate from the list, no restart |
| Label | Unmanaged | **Shaderpack: GLSL only. It contains no Java.** |
| Updates | The mod copies the files again | The player sees a dot and the **Changelog** tab |

## The procedure

1. Make the folder `media/viewpoint/shaderpacks/<id>/` in your mod. Put it in `common/`, or in the version folder.
2. Move your `pack.properties` and your `shaders/` folder into it. Add `textures/` if the pack has images.
3. Add the package keys to `pack.properties`: `format`, `id`, `version` and `game.min`. Add `icon`, `license` and
   `changelog` if you can. See [Format](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/shaderpacks/format.md).
4. Make the folder name the same as the `id`.
5. Remove the installer jar. Remove `javaJarFile` from `mod.info`. Keep `require=Viewpoint`.
6. Remove the code that copied files. Nothing copies the pack now.
7. Switch the mod on. Open **Graphics**, **Shaderpacks**. Find the card of your pack.
8. Put the pointer on the card and click the green tick, or double-click the card. Accept the dialog. Look at the picture.

## The id

A package id uses lower-case letters, digits, `.` and `-`. The name of an old folder pack can use capital letters and `_`.
If your old name is not a correct id, choose a new id.

The options of the pack are saved as `pack.<encoded id>.<option>`. If the encoded id of the new package is the same as the
old name of the folder pack, the saved options of the player stay. If it is not the same, the player sets the options
again. See [Package kinds](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/package-kinds.md#the-encoded-id).

## If the player still has the old copy

An old copy in `Zomboid/viewpoint-shaderpacks/` stays in the player's folder. When its name and author are the same as
those of your package, the card of the old copy says "a packaged version is installed". Tell the player in your
changelog to delete the old folder.

## If the pack builds on another pack

Put `base=` in `pack.properties`. If the base is a Shaderpack of another mod, add it to `requires`. See
[Format](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/shaderpacks/format.md#build-on-another-pack).

## If your jar also changed library GLSL

Some jars also patched `Shaders.read` to change library GLSL as the game starts. A Shaderpack does this with files in
`shaders/`. A small change that must apply under any pack is a shader snippet. See
[Migrating from ZombieBuddy](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/migrating-from-zombiebuddy.md).

> **Note**
>
> The player sees the shader line on the card: "Has shader code: Viewpoint checks its size and form. Faulty shader code can
> stall or crash the graphics driver." Viewpoint cannot check what GLSL computes. Test your pack on more than one graphics
> card if you can.

---

# Managing addons

> For players. Install addons and resource packs, turn them on and off, put them in order, and see what they do.

Addons and resource packs add to Viewpoint, and you stay in charge of them from the settings window. You can turn any of
them on or off while you play, without restarting the game, and you can see what each one does before you say yes.

You'll find them in two places:

- **Addons** are in **Advanced**, **Addons**.
- **Resource packs** are in **Graphics**, **Resource Packs**.

Shaderpacks work a little differently and have [their own page](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/players/shaderpacks.md).

## Install an addon

1. Get the mod that contains the addon, usually from the Steam Workshop.
2. Enable that mod and Viewpoint in the game's mod list.
3. Start the game. Viewpoint only looks for addons in mods that were on when the game started. If an addon offers
   functions to Lua, you may see "Viewpoint is checking N addons" for a few seconds.
4. Open the settings window and go to **Advanced**, **Addons**.
5. Your new addon is in the **Inactive** column. Every new addon starts there, so nothing runs until you choose.

## Find your way around the page

The page has a search box and two columns. **Inactive** on the left holds what's installed but off. **Active** on the
right holds what's on, with the top card going first.

Each card shows the name, a description and a line like `v1.2.0 · by Someone`. If a description gets cut off, rest the
pointer on it for a couple of seconds to read the rest. A grey square just means the author didn't include a picture.

Point at a card and its buttons appear:

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Green tick, where the picture was (Inactive) | Turns it on |
| Red minus, where the picture was (Active) | Turns it off |
| **Info**, top right | Shows everything about the addon |
| **Settings**, the cog at the bottom right (only when active) | Opens the addon's own settings |

Double-clicking a card also turns it on or off.

Beside the search box, **Addon VRAM Usage** adds up the video memory your active addons asked for when they started. It's
what they're allowed to use, not what they're using right now, and Viewpoint doesn't put a limit on it. An addon that
draws and doesn't name an amount counts as 64 MiB.

If Viewpoint refuses something, such as turning on an addon when an addon it needs is off, a line at the top of the page
tells you why and then fades after a few seconds.

Two small marks are worth knowing. A **dot** beside the name means the addon has changed since you accepted it. A **word**
beside the name, such as **Suspended**, means it's in a state other than plain on or off. Point at the word to find out why.

## Turn an addon on

1. Click the green tick, or double-click the card.
2. Read the dialog. It shows the addon's label, the reasons for that label, and everything the addon asks for. Long lists
   scroll, and nothing is ever cut.
3. To say no, click **Cancel** or press **Esc**. To say yes, wait for **Accept** to light up, rest the pointer on it for a
   moment, and click.
4. The card moves to the **Active** column.

The short wait on **Accept** is deliberate, so that a stray click can't agree to something you haven't read. If the addon
changes on disk while you're reading, Viewpoint shows you the dialog again.

A **Red** addon asks twice: after **Accept...** you get a second button, **Switch on a Red addon**, with the same wait.
That's because a Red addon can do things outside Viewpoint's control.

Your yes covers that version only. If an update asks for more, Viewpoint asks you again.

Viewpoint remembers what was on and in what order, and turns it all back on next time you start the game. There are two
exceptions. An addon that needs your consent again stays off until you click its green tick, and an addon that **Failed** to
start isn't tried again automatically.

## Turn an addon off

Click the red minus or double-click the card. The addon stops straight away. Any hooks it put into the game come out at the
next safe moment, which is the main menu, a loading screen, or a paused single-player game with the window open. The card
tells you when that has happened.

## Choose the order

Drag a card up or down in the **Active** column, or use the arrows on its left. An arrow is dim when the card can't go any
further that way. When you drag, drop on the top half of another card to land above it, or the bottom half to land below it.

Order matters when two addons want the same thing. If they change the same model, tile or hook, the one nearer the top
wins. Some things can only belong to one addon at a time, like the camera or the reticle. The addon nearer the top gets it,
and the other addon's card tells you who has it. [Order](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/order.md) has the details.

## See what an addon does

Click **Info** on the card to get these tabs:

| Tab | What you'll find |
| --- | --- |
| Overview | The description, the author, and the versions it supports |
| Trust | Its label and why it got it, what it does with Lua and shaders, its signature, and the ZombieBuddy policy |
| Permissions | What it asks for |
| Hooks | Each place it hooks into the game or Viewpoint, how often that runs, how long it takes, and how many calls were skipped |
| Files | Its folder, its storage limit, and what it downloaded this session |
| Changelog | What changed since you accepted it, and the author's own notes |
| Performance | What it costs to run |

Many addons also have a settings page, behind the cog on an active card. Some split it into sections. Click a title at the
top of the page to switch between them.

### Block a single hook

If one hook is causing trouble, you can block just that one and keep the rest of the addon.

1. Open **Info**, then **Hooks**.
2. Find the hook and click **Veto**.

From the next safe moment, the game runs as if the addon never had that hook. **Allow again** undoes it.

## What the labels mean

Every addon gets a label from Viewpoint's automatic check of its Java code. It describes what the check found in this
version. It isn't a promise about what the code will do, and Lua isn't checked at all.

| Label | How it looks | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Normal** | Like any other card | The code only uses parts of Viewpoint that have been reviewed. |
| **Amber** | Amber name and icon | The code uses things that haven't been reviewed, which includes drawing with OpenGL. Turn it on if you trust the author. |
| **Red** | Red name and icon, on a red card | The code can do things outside Viewpoint's control. It stays off until you allow it, so only do that for authors you trust. |

Point at the icon or the name to read what the label means. The full wording is on the
[Labels](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/trust/labels.md#the-texts-that-the-player-sees) page.

A card may also tell you that an addon draws over the whole screen, or that any mod's Lua can call its Java. It's worth
reading those lines before you turn it on.

You might also see two other marks. **Unmanaged** is a mod that loads its own Java outside Viewpoint, so Viewpoint can't
turn it off or show you what it does. **Cannot be checked** is an addon that Viewpoint couldn't check, so it won't start.

## What the states mean

| State | What's going on |
| --- | --- |
| Incompatible | It doesn't match your game or your version of Viewpoint. The card says which version it needs. |
| Refused | Its files are wrong, or its requirements go round in a circle. It won't start, and the card says why. |
| Inactive | It's off. If the card gives a reason, something is holding it back, like a required package that's off. |
| Checking | Viewpoint is checking the jar and its signature in the background. It carries on when that's done. |
| Awaiting consent | You clicked the green tick, and it's waiting for your answer. |
| Active | It's on. |
| Active: hooks pending | It's on, and its hooks go into the game at the next safe moment. |
| Failed | It didn't start. The card says why. |
| Suspended | Viewpoint stopped it for this session, because it hit an error or the server doesn't list it. Turn it on again to restart it. |
| Needs an update | It uses a part of Viewpoint that no longer exists, so it won't start. Ask the author for an update. |

## Accept an update

When an addon updates, its card gets a **dot**. Click **Info** and open **Changelog** to see the author's notes and a list
of what changed, with a mark on anything that asks for more than before.

- **If it asks for more,** the addon stays off and the card says why. Click the green tick to read the dialog and accept.
  The dot goes away when you accept.
- **If it doesn't,** the addon keeps running as it was. It picks up the new files the next time you turn it on or restart
  the game. Until then the card says *Update available. It applies at the next enable or restart.* The dot goes away once
  you've opened **Info**.

## Downloads

An addon has to ask you before **every** download. The dialog shows the addon's ID and name, the host, the full address,
where the file will be saved, and its size. The file's real extension is picked out in orange, so `photo.png.exe` can't pass
itself off as a picture.

Nothing is kept until you click **Accept**. If you click **Deny** too many times, the addon can't ask again until you
restart the game. You can see each download in the addon's **Files** tab.

## Check what an addon costs

**Info**, **Performance** shows the memory and video memory the addon uses next to what Viewpoint estimated from its files,
how long its hooks and drawing take, and its history over your last 8 sessions.

To measure its cost on your graphics card, click **Measure GPU cost**. For about 20 seconds Viewpoint draws the addon's
models and hides them in turn, so stay still until it finishes. The result carries over to later sessions.

The history stays in a file on your computer and never leaves it. **Clear the usage file** deletes the history of all addons.

## Resource packs

Resource packs change models and art, and contain no code. They live in **Graphics**, **Resource Packs**, and the page works
just like the Addons page, with the same two columns, the same buttons and the same ordering. If two packs change the same
sprite, the one nearer the top wins. Older Viewpoint model packs appear here too, with a *legacy* flag.

## Playing on a server

- Addons that only change what you see or hear (`side=client`) stay on when you join a server.
- Addons that change gameplay (`side=gameplay`) are **Suspended** if the server doesn't list them.
- Hooks only go into the game at the main menu or on a loading screen.

> **Note**
>
> Viewpoint shows a disclaimer in the settings window and the first time you turn on an addon. Please read it before you turn
> one on.

---

# Shaderpacks

> For players. Find a Shaderpack, turn it on, and understand what its card tells you.

A Shaderpack changes the whole look of the game: the light, the sky, the colours and the effects. It's made of graphics code
and contains no Java. You'll find them in the settings window under **Graphics**, **Shaderpacks**.

## What's on the page

Every pack you have is in one list:

- the packs that come with Viewpoint;
- Viewpoint packs and Minecraft shader packs you've put in `Zomboid/viewpoint-shaderpacks/`;
- Shaderpacks that came in a mod. These ask for your consent first.

The pack you're using sits at the top in green. Only one pack can draw the world at a time. Each card shows the name, a
description, and the version and author, and there's a search box above the list.

Added a Minecraft pack while the game is running? Click the **Rescan** button beside the search box to pick it up.

## Use a Shaderpack

1. Enable Viewpoint in the game's mod list, along with the mod the pack came in if it came in one, then start the game.
2. Open **Graphics**, **Shaderpacks**.
3. Point at the pack's card and click the green tick, or double-click the card.
4. If the pack came in a mod, read the dialog and accept it.

To stop using a pack, just activate another one. The pack's own options are in **Graphics**, **Shader Options**.

A Shaderpack redraws the whole frame, so it can cost your graphics card far more than an addon does. The
[Cost](#cost) section shows how to check.

## If your pack gets turned off

If you switch off the package for the pack you're using, or its mod gets removed, Viewpoint falls back to the `default` pack
for the moment and the **Graphics** page tells you why. Your choice stays saved, so your pack comes back as soon as you turn
it on again.

## What the card might say

| The card says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Waiting for \<pack\>** | This pack builds on another pack that isn't on yet. Turn that one on. |
| **Inactive: requires its base** | The mod doesn't say which pack this one builds on. Ask the author. |
| **A packaged version is installed** | A pack in your folder has the same name and author as one from a mod. You can delete the copy in your folder. |
| **Made for \<version\>: N of the files it replaces have changed since** (planned) | The pack was made for an older Viewpoint. It may still work, but some effects can look different. |

## Reading the label

A Shaderpack's label says **Shaderpack: GLSL only. It contains no Java.** It also shows the pack's licence, or **No licence
given**. There's a second line too:

> Has shader code: Viewpoint checks its size and form. Faulty shader code can stall or crash the graphics driver.

Viewpoint can't check what graphics code actually computes. If a pack makes the game stall or crash, switch to the `default`
pack on the same page.

## Cost

While a pack with passes of its own is in use, a line above the list shows what it costs: the video memory its own targets
use, and the time its passes take on your graphics card each frame, broken down by stage. The time is an average over about
the last second. For a pack from a mod, **Info**, **Performance** shows the same line.

For the full picture, compare your frame rate against the **Default** pack. If you'd like more detail, see
[Measuring your addon](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/performance/measuring-your-addon.md).

> **Tip**
>
> If a pack runs slowly on your graphics card, try a lower setting in its Quality list, or turn some effects off in
> **Shader Options**.

Addons and resource packs are covered in [Managing addons](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/players/managing-addons.md).

---

# API reference

> The packages of viewpoint.api, and where to find the javadoc.

Each Viewpoint release has `viewpoint-api.jar`, with a sources jar and a javadoc jar. The javadoc gives each public type
and member of `viewpoint.api`. It has:

- a description of each type and member;
- a `@thread` tag on each method, which tells the thread that can call it;
- the API version, the same as `Version.API`.

## Packages

| Package | Contains | Guide |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `viewpoint.api` | `Addon`, `AddonContext`, `Registration`, `Version`, `AddonRender`, `AddonShaders`, `AddonSnippets` | [Getting started](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/start/getting-started.md) |
| `viewpoint.api.patch` | `@Hook.Before`, `@Hook.After`, `HookCall` | [Managed patching](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/patching/managed-patching.md) |
| `viewpoint.api.view` | `ViewState`, `ViewListener` | [View state](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/view-state.md) |
| `viewpoint.api.settings` | `AddonSettings`, `KeyAction`, `SettingsPage` | [Settings & keys](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/settings-and-keys.md) |
| `viewpoint.api.files` | `AddonFiles`, `Pending` | [Files](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/files.md) |
| `viewpoint.api.net` | `AddonDownloads`, `DownloadRequest`, `DownloadResult` | [Downloads](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/downloads.md) |
| `viewpoint.api.assets` | `AddonAssets` | [Assets](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/assets.md) |
| `viewpoint.api.lua` | `@LuaExport`, `LuaTable`, `LuaHandle` | [Lua exports](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/lua-exports.md) |
| `viewpoint.api.services` | `Services` | [Services](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/services.md) |
| `viewpoint.api.camera` | `AddonCamera`, `CameraLayer`, `LookControl`, `CameraClaim`, `ViewControl`, `CursorClaim` | [Camera layers](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/camera-layers.md) |
| `viewpoint.api.combat` | `AddonCombat`, `AimListener`, `AimState`, `ShotListener`, `ShotEvent`, `ShotHit`, `SwayProvider`, `Sway`, `ShotResolver`, `ResolverClaim`, `ReticleProvider`, `Reticle`, `ReticleImage`, `ReticleClaim` | [Aim & shots](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/aim-and-shots.md) |
| `viewpoint.api.models` | `ModelProvider`, `AttachmentProvider`, `ModelRef` | [Model providers](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/model-providers.md) |
| `viewpoint.api.render` | `DrawPoint`, `DrawCallback`, `DrawContext`, `FrameView`, `Gpu` (`GpuProgram`, `GpuBuffer`, `GpuTexture`, `GpuMesh`), `Picture`, `Primitive`, `FrameInput`, `ShaderValues`, `ShaderValue`, `ShaderPulse`, `ValueKind`, `SnippetPoint` | [Draw callbacks](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/draw-callbacks.md), [Shader values](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/shader-values.md), [Shader snippets](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/shader-snippets.md) |

The API uses only `java.*` and `viewpoint.api.*`. `viewpoint-api.jar` has the MIT licence.

## Lua

| Function | Guide |
| --- | --- |
| `Viewpoint.Addons.viewState()` | [Lua mirror](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/lua-mirror.md) |
| `Viewpoint.Addons.terrainHeight(x, y)` | [Lua mirror](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/lua-mirror.md) |
| `Viewpoint.Addons.setting(addonId, name)` | [Lua mirror](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/lua-mirror.md) |
| `Viewpoint.Addons["<id>"]` and the globals of `lua.globals` | [Lua exports](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/lua-exports.md) |
| `Viewpoint.ModelPacks.register(modId, path)` | [Legacy model packs](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/resource-packs/legacy-model-packs.md) |

# Descriptor keys

> All keys of addon.properties and pack.properties in one table.

All descriptor keys in one table. The [Descriptor](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/descriptor.md) page explains them. `A` is an addon. `P` is a
resource pack. `S` is a Shaderpack.

| Key | For | Required | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `format` | A P S | Yes | | The format of the descriptor: `1`. |
| `id` | A P S | Yes | | The id. The folder name must be the same. |
| `name` | A P S | Yes | | The name on the card. |
| `version` | A P S | Yes | | The version: major, minor and patch, each of at most three digits (`MMM.NNN.PPP`). |
| `author` | A P S | No | | The author on the card. |
| `description` | A P S | No | | A short description, at most 128 characters. The card shows the start of it; the player reads all of it when the pointer rests on it. |
| `icon` | A P S | No | A tile with a letter | A PNG file in the package folder. |
| `license` | A P S | No | | The name of the licence. |
| `game.min` | A P S | Yes | | The oldest game build. |
| `game.max` | A P S | No | No limit | The newest game build. |
| `viewpoint.min` | A P S | No | | The oldest Viewpoint version. |
| `viewpoint.max` | A P S | No | No limit | The newest Viewpoint version. |
| `side` | A | No | `client` | `client` or `gameplay`. |
| `requires` | A P S | No | | `id` or `id@min`, with commas between them. |
| `conflicts` | A P S | No | | Ids, with commas between them. |
| `changelog` | A P S | No | | A file of `## <version>` sections. |
| `models` | A P | No | | The path of a model manifest. Use version 2; version 1 is deprecated. |
| `tiles` | A P | No | | A folder of tile PNG files. |
| `sounds` | A P | No | | A folder of `ogg` and `wav` files. |
| `data` | A P | No | | A folder of data files. |
| `api` | A | Yes | | The API version that you compiled against: `1.0`. |
| `jar` | A | Yes | | The name of the jar. |
| `entry` | A | Yes | | The class that implements `Addon`. |
| `settings` | A | No | | A `settings.properties` file. |
| `permissions` | A | No | None | `hooks`, `files`, `downloads`, `lua`, `camera`, `combat`, `models`, `shaders`, `draw`, `vram`. |
| `hooks.targets` | A | With `hooks` | | The classes that the addon can hook: game classes and listed classes of Viewpoint. |
| `files.quotaMiB` | A | No | 64 | The size of the files folder, in MiB. More than 64 needs consent. |
| `draw.gpuMiB` | A | No | 64 | The video memory for the `Gpu` objects, in MiB, 1 or more. It needs `draw`. More than 128 needs the permission `vram`. |
| `downloads.hosts` | A | With `downloads` | | The hosts that the addon can download from. |
| `lua.globals` | A | No | | Names of Lua globals for the exports. |
| `exports` | A | No | | Java packages that other addons can link to. |
| `base` | S | No | The library | The pack that the Shaderpack builds on. |
| `dropOptions` | S | No | | Options of the base that the pack leaves out. |
| `options`, `option.<id>.*` | S | No | | The options of the pack. |
| `presets`, `preset.<id>`, `preset.default` | S | No | | The presets of the pack. |
| `passes`, `pass.<id>.*`, `targets`, `target.<name>` | S | No | | The passes and targets of the pack. |
| `pipeline.<knob>` | S | No | The base | Which passes of the renderer run. |
| `library` | S | No | | The Viewpoint version that the pack was made for (planned). |

---

# Labels

> The label levels, their reasons and the texts that the player sees.

The [Labels](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/trust/labels.md) page explains the labels. This page gives the texts and the reasons in tables.

## Texts

In Amber and Red, the braces show a list. The card shows only the items that apply, with " · " between them.

| Name | Text |
| --- | --- |
| Normal (no badge; its tooltip) | Checked by Viewpoint. This addon's Java code uses only parts of Java, the game and Viewpoint that Viewpoint has reviewed. Viewpoint found no way for it to reach your files outside its own folder, the internet, other programs or native code. It can still change anything in your game and saves. In multiplayer, what it puts into the game is sent to the server. The mod's Lua scripts are not checked. Its assets are checked for their form and size, not for what they do. |
| Amber | Uses things Viewpoint has not reviewed: \{background threads · multiplayer messages · Lua · draws with OpenGL · internals of Viewpoint · hooks that run on any thread · other parts of Java and the game · code of other addons\}. Viewpoint cannot tell what these lead to. Turn it on only if you trust the author. |
| Red (off until allowed) | Can \{read and write your files · reach the internet · start programs · load native code · change the game's code · reach any part of the game by name · stop the game or change settings of the whole game · read and write any memory of the game · use OpenGL outside the draw callbacks · use internals of Viewpoint that are graded Red · hook the render thread · do what the addons it links to can do\}. Viewpoint cannot protect you from what this addon does. Allow it only for authors you trust. |
| Disclaimer (the settings page, and the first enable) | Labels describe what Viewpoint's automatic check found in this version of the addon's Java code. They are not a promise of safety: a check can miss things, and an addon can misbehave within what it is allowed. Addons are made by third parties. Viewpoint's authors do not review, endorse or answer for them. |
| Unmanaged (amber) | Unmanaged: runs outside Viewpoint's controls (hooks cannot be listed, ordered or vetoed) |
| Unmanaged, red | loads before Viewpoint |
| Resource pack | Resource pack: assets only. Viewpoint read these files with its own loaders and found them within its limits. It contains no Java. |
| Shaderpack | Shaderpack: GLSL only. It contains no Java. (With the licence of the pack, or "No licence given".) |
| Shader line (a Shaderpack, and an addon with snippets or `Gpu` programs) | Has shader code: Viewpoint checks its size and form. Faulty shader code can stall or crash the graphics driver. |
| Export line (adds to the Lua line) | any mod's Lua can call N functions of its Java; they use: \{permissions\} |
| Export line, one function | any mod's Lua can call 1 function of its Java; it uses: \{permissions\} |
| Lua line | Has Lua: not checked by Viewpoint |
| Lua line, with what was found | Has Lua: not checked by Viewpoint. Found in it: \{names\} |
| Lua line, no Lua | No Lua |
| Too large or too complex | Cannot be checked |

The items of the lists:

| Level | Items |
| --- | --- |
| Amber | background threads · multiplayer messages · Lua · draws with OpenGL · internals of Viewpoint · hooks that run on any thread · other parts of Java and the game · code of other addons |
| Red | read and write your files · reach the internet · start programs · load native code · change the game's code · reach any part of the game by name · stop the game or change settings of the whole game · read and write any memory of the game · use OpenGL outside the draw callbacks · use internals of Viewpoint that are graded Red · hook the render thread · do what the addons it links to can do |

## The export line

The words after "they use:" or "it uses:" are the items that the exported functions reach. These are all the items:

threads · the server · Lua · files · the network · programs · native code · classes · reflection · the game's process · memory · OpenGL · internals of Viewpoint · hooks · parts of the game · other addons

If the functions reach none of them, the line says "nothing that Viewpoint lists".

The line counts the functions that the exports call. It does not count code that runs when a class loads, or an object
that the addon stored for later.

## Reasons

| Level | The addon |
| --- | --- |
| Amber | Starts background threads |
| Amber | Sends multiplayer messages |
| Amber | Calls Lua |
| Amber | Draws with OpenGL in a draw callback |
| Amber | Uses internals of Viewpoint that are graded Amber |
| Amber | Uses deprecated internals |
| Amber | Uses parts of Java or the game that Viewpoint has not reviewed |
| Amber | Extends a class that Viewpoint has not reviewed |
| Amber | Has a hook with `thread = ANY` |
| Amber | Has a costly hook (a method that the game calls very frequently) |
| Amber | Has a slow hook (a handler that takes too much time) |
| Amber | Uses code of X (Amber) |
| Red | Reads or writes files, or uses code of the game that does |
| Red | Opens network connections, or uses code of the game that does |
| Red | Uses reflection |
| Red | Starts programs |
| Red | Loads native code |
| Red | Defines classes |
| Red | Uses OpenGL directly, outside the draw callbacks and the allowed calls |
| Red | Uses LWJGL, which can read and write any memory of the game |
| Red | Stops the game process, or changes settings of the full Java process |
| Red | Uses internals of Viewpoint that are graded Red |
| Red | Has a hook with `thread = RENDER` |
| Red | Uses code of X (Red) |

A Red reason that a Lua export can reach ends with "…, callable from any mod's Lua".

## Other lines of a card

| Line | When |
| --- | --- |
| Draws over the whole screen | The addon draws at the `final` point or the `crosshair` point. |
| Its Lua functions came late at this start | The addon was not ready before the limit at the start of the game. |
| The shaderpack X has no point Y | A Shaderpack does not keep a marker, and a snippet of this addon needs it. |
| Made for \<version\>: N of the files it replaces have changed since (planned) | A Shaderpack is older than the files that it replaces. |
| Needs an update: uses \<member\>, removed in \<release\>; use \<replacement\> | The addon uses a member of Viewpoint that is gone. |
| Needs an update: uses \<member\>, removed in \<release\>; nothing replaces it | The addon uses a member of Viewpoint that is gone, and no other member does the same. |

## The Lua line

`Has Lua: not checked by Viewpoint`, then `Found in it:` and the names that Viewpoint found in the Lua of the mod, for
example `getModFileWriter`, `getHostByName` or `Clipboard`. Or `No Lua`.

Viewpoint lists these names. Some write, read or list files: `getFileWriter`, `getModFileWriter`, `getFileReader`,
`getModFileReader`, `getFileInput`, `getFileOutput`, `getGameFilesInput`, `getGameFilesTextInput`,
`listFilesInModDirectory`, `listFilesInZomboidLuaDirectory`, `serverFileExists` and `cacheFileExists`. Some reach the
internet or the desktop: `getHostByName`, `openUrl`, `activateSteamOverlayToWebPage`, `showFolderInDesktop` and
`Clipboard`. Some load a file as code or make code, or a global, from text or bytes, which hides it from this check:
`loadstring`, `bytecodeloader`, `reloadLuaFile`, `reloadServerLuaFile`, `rawset`, `setfenv` and `getfenv`. Viewpoint
reads the Lua as text. It does not run it, and it cannot see a name that the Lua makes from other text.

---

# Permissions

> The permissions, their keys and their limits, in one table.

The [Permissions](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/trust/permissions.md) page explains the permissions.

| Permission | Keys | Limits | Without it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hooks` | `hooks.targets` | Some targets are refused. `thread = ANY` has rules. Viewpoint measures the time of each handler. | The addon cannot start. |
| `files` | `files.quotaMiB` | 64 MiB for each folder by default, 16 MiB for each file, 1,000 files | Each call gives a `SecurityException`. |
| `downloads` | `downloads.hosts` | `https` only, hosts from `downloads.hosts`, 256 MiB for each file, the player accepts each download | Each call gives a `SecurityException`. |
| `lua` | `lua.globals` | Calls run on the main thread. A global must be free. | Viewpoint refuses the jar. |
| `camera` | None | One claim at a time for the camera, the view and the cursor. | Each call gives a `SecurityException`. |
| `combat` | None | One shot resolver and one reticle at a time. | Each call gives a `SecurityException`. |
| `models` | None | Providers answer on the main thread, for the sprites that they name. | Each call gives a `SecurityException`. |
| `shaders` | None | Snippets have size limits. Values are set on the main thread. | Each call gives a `SecurityException`. |
| `draw` | `draw.gpuMiB` | Drawing only in a draw callback. A limited list of OpenGL calls. 64 MiB of video memory by default, 128 MiB at most. | Each call gives a `SecurityException`. |
| `vram` | `draw.gpuMiB` | More than 128 MiB of video memory for the `Gpu` objects. Viewpoint sets no limit. | More than 128 in `draw.gpuMiB` makes the descriptor wrong. |

These need no permission:

- the view state;
- the settings of the addon, its settings page and its key bindings;
- the assets of the addon;
- services.

A new permission, a new target, a new host, a new export or a larger quota needs the player's consent again. See
[Updates & changelogs](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/trust/updates-and-changelogs.md).

---

# Internals changes

> What each Viewpoint release adds to, deprecates in and removes from the internals list, with the replacements.

Viewpoint changes in each release. The [internals list](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/reference/viewpoint-internals.md) changes with it. This page lists
the changes of the list, release by release, so that you can update your addon.

Viewpoint writes this page when it builds a release. Do not edit it by hand.

## What the page lists

For each release, the page has three tables.

| Table | Meaning | What you do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Added** | New members on the list. | Nothing. You can use them. |
| **Deprecated** | Members that still work and will go. The table names the replacement. | Move to the replacement. The card of your addon shows **uses deprecated internals** until you do. |
| **Removed** | Members that are gone. The table names the release and the replacement. | Update your addon. It shows **Needs an update** and does not start until you do. |

Each row gives the class, the member, the release and, for the last two tables, the replacement.

# Glossary

> The terms that these pages use. Each term has one meaning on all pages.

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Addon** | A package with Java code, described by `addon.properties`. It can also contain assets, shader snippets and Lua. |
| **Resource Pack** | A package with assets only (models, tiles, sounds, data), described by `pack.properties`. It has no Java and no shader code. |
| **Shaderpack** | A package with GLSL files and their options, described by `pack.properties`. It has no Java. It changes how Viewpoint draws the world. |
| **Package** | An addon, a resource pack or a Shaderpack. |
| **Base** | The pack that a Shaderpack builds on, named by `base=`. |
| **Encoded id** | An id with `.` and `-` written as `_`. It is used in settings keys and in GLSL names. |
| **Descriptor** | The file that describes a package: `addon.properties` or `pack.properties`. |
| **Hook** | A declaration in your jar that connects a handler to a game method. Viewpoint installs it. |
| **Handler** | Your `public static` method that Viewpoint runs before or after the hooked game method. |
| **Kind** | What a handler can do: `OBSERVE`, `ARGS`, `RETURN` or `SKIP`. |
| **Permission** | A service that an addon asks for in `permissions`: `hooks`, `files`, `downloads`, `lua`, `camera`, `combat`, `models`, `shaders` or `draw`. |
| **Label** | The result of Viewpoint's automatic check, on the card: **Normal**, **Amber** or **Red**. |
| **Lua line** | The last line of each label. It tells if the package has Lua. Viewpoint does not check Lua. |
| **Shader line** | A line of a card that says that the package has shader code. Viewpoint checks its size and form, not what it computes. |
| **Export** | A Java function of an addon that the Lua of any mod can call. |
| **Service** | An object that an addon publishes under an id, so that other addons can use it. |
| **Camera layer** | A small change that an addon adds to the camera. Many layers can be active together. |
| **Claim** | A right that only one addon at a time can hold, for example the camera, the cursor or the reticle. The addon nearer the top of the Active column wins. |
| **Provider** | An object that an addon gives to Viewpoint to choose the model of a world object or of a character. |
| **Shader value** | A number that an addon sets, and that shader code reads as `uAddon_<encoded id>_<name>`. |
| **Snippet** | A small piece of GLSL that an addon adds at a named point of a shader. |
| **Draw callback** | A function of an addon that Viewpoint calls at a named point of a frame, so that the addon can draw. |
| **Internals list** | The members of Viewpoint outside `viewpoint.api` that an addon can use or hook. |
| **Consent** | The player's acceptance of one version of one package. An update that asks for more needs consent again. |
| **Card** | The row that shows one package in the settings window. |
| **Active column** | The list of the packages that are on. The package nearer the top wins. |
| **Safe point** | A time when Viewpoint can install and remove hooks: the main menu, a loading screen, or a paused single-player game. |
| **Registration** | An object that the API gives you for a listener or a callback. Viewpoint closes it when the addon goes off. |
| **Legacy** | A flag for an older Viewpoint model pack. It is a resource pack. |
| **Unmanaged** | A flag for a mod that loads its Java through ZombieBuddy (`javaJarFile`). Viewpoint does not control it. |
| **Gone** | A member of Viewpoint that a release removed. An addon that uses it shows **Needs an update**. |
| **Suspended** | The state of an addon that Viewpoint stopped for the session, after an error or on a server that does not list it. |
| **Pool** | A part of memory with a maximum size, for one kind of asset. |

---

# Shader snippets

> An addon adds a small piece of GLSL at a named point of a shader.

A snippet is a small piece of GLSL that your addon adds at a named point of the shaders of Viewpoint. Use it to change a
surface, a vertex or a colour, for example to make surfaces wet or to tint the scene.

**Permission:** `shaders`.

```properties
permissions=shaders
```

## Add a snippet

A snippet is the body of a function. Viewpoint declares the function for the point, with the point's parameters. Your
snippet reads and changes the parameters.

```java title="WetPart.java"
AddonSnippets snippets = ctx.shaders().snippets();
ShaderValue wetness = ctx.shaders().values().declare("wetness", ValueKind.FLOAT);

snippets.add(SnippetPoint.GBUFFER_END, "wet", """
        g.albedo.rgb *= 1.0 - 0.4 * wetness;
        """);
```

- `add` takes the point, a name for messages, the body, and the programs that it runs in. Give no program to run it in
  every program that has the point.
- Load a long snippet from your data assets, then add it. See [Assets](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/assets.md).
- Close the registration to take the snippet out. When your addon goes off, Viewpoint takes out all its snippets.
- Read the values of your addon by their names, for example `wetness` above. See [Shader values](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/api/shader-values.md).

## The points

| Point | Parameters | Programs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `surface` | `inout Surface s` (`vec3 albedo`, `vec3 normal`, `vec4 light`, `bool foliage`), `vec3 local`, `vec3 pos`, `vec3 eye` | `gbuffer`, `forward`, `far shell`, `far shell band` |
| `vertex.world` | `inout MeshVertex v` (`v.pos` in scene space) | `gbuffer`, `forward`, `puddle` |
| `vertex.end` | `inout vec4 clipPosition` | every program with a vertex stage, but those with tessellation or a geometry stage |
| `gbuffer.end` | `inout GBuffer g` (`vec4 albedo`, `vec4 normal`, `vec4 light`, `vec4 velocity`) | `gbuffer`, `far shell band`, `model`, `vehicle`, `grass`, `snow layer`, `snow layer tessellated`, `snow wake` |
| `colour.end` | `inout vec4 colour` | `light`, `far shell`, `far` |

`surface` and `vertex.world` are in the middle of a shader. A Shaderpack that replaces their file keeps their marker. If a
Shaderpack does not keep it, your snippets at that point do not run, and a message on the Addons page says so.

At `gbuffer.end`, a program without a velocity output ignores what you write to `g.velocity`.

## Rules

Viewpoint checks each snippet when you add it. If the snippet breaks a rule, `add` throws an
`IllegalArgumentException` that gives each reason.

- A snippet is at most 16 KiB. The snippets of one addon are at most 64 KiB together.
- The braces, brackets and parentheses of a snippet close in the snippet.
- A snippet has no `#` lines.
- A snippet has no `while` or `do` loops. A `for` loop counts with numbers towards a number:
  `for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++)`, or `for (int i = 8; i > 0; i -= 2)`.
- A snippet writes no images or buffers, and calls no atomic or barrier functions. It declares no uniforms or blocks.
- A snippet uses none of the names of Viewpoint's shaders: no name of `u`, `v` or `a` followed by a capital letter, and no
  name that starts with `vp_` or `addon_`. Of the names that start with `gl_`, it can read only `gl_FragCoord`,
  `gl_FrontFacing`, `gl_PointCoord`, `gl_VertexID` and `gl_InstanceID`.

The graphics driver compiles the snippet. If it fails, your snippets at that point stop, a message on the Addons page
says so, and `console.txt` has the driver's error. The other addons and Viewpoint go on.

## When a change applies

When an addon with snippets goes on or off, Viewpoint compiles the programs with those points again.

- In a single-player game, the game pauses until the programs are ready. A dark layer covers the screen, under the Esc
  menu, and the bar at the bottom left shows "Compiling addon shaders" and the progress.
- In a multiplayer game, the game does not pause. Only the bar shows.

> **Note**
>
> After the programs are ready, a snippet costs only its own GPU time in each frame. Your card's Performance tab shows it.

---

# Draw callbacks

> An addon draws with OpenGL at a named point of a frame.

An addon can draw with OpenGL at a named point of the frame. The card of such an addon says that it draws with OpenGL.

**Permission:** `draw`. More than 128 MiB of video memory also needs `vram`.

```properties
permissions=draw
draw.gpuMiB=32
```

## Points

| Point | When | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AFTER_OPAQUE` | The opaque world and its light are drawn. The glass and the water are not drawn yet. | The colour of the frame in high dynamic range, with the depth of the world |
| `AFTER_TRANSLUCENT` | The glass and the other translucent things are blended in. | The same |
| `AFTER_WEATHER` | The wet ground, the puddles and the distant rain are drawn, or none was necessary. | The same |
| `BEFORE_POST` | The world is complete. The light in the air, the bloom and the tone mapping come next. | The same |
| `CROSSHAIR` | Where the crosshair goes, only while the crosshair shows. | The screen |
| `FINAL` | The final picture is on the screen, with its colours as shown, before the interface of the game. | The screen |

- No point runs while a Minecraft shader pack draws the frame. The pack owns its targets.
- At one point, the callbacks of the addons run in the order of the player. See [Order](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/concepts/order.md).
- What you draw at `AFTER_OPAQUE` to `BEFORE_POST` goes through the post-processing of Viewpoint. Write the depth too, if
  you draw into the world: the light in the air goes over a pixel that has the depth of the sky.

```java title="MarkerPart.java"
ctx.render().draw(DrawPoint.FINAL, context -> {
    FrameView view = context.view(); // the matrices, the eye, the origin of scene space
    int width = context.width();     // the size of the target that is bound
    // Draw here, on the render thread.
});
```

## The frame's view

`DrawContext.view()` gives a `FrameView`:

- `view()` and `projection()`: the matrices of the frame, 16 numbers by columns. The projection is the one that the world
  is drawn with in this frame, with the offset of the anti-aliasing.
- `eye()`: the place of the eye in scene space.
- `sceneOrigin()`: the point of the world that is the origin of scene space. In scene space, `x` points west, `y` up in
  squares (a storey is about 2.45 squares) and `z` north.
- `frameWidth()`, `frameHeight()`: the size of the targets of the frame before the post-processing.
- `seconds()`: the clock of the scene.

## The state that you leave

A callback runs on the render thread. Draw into the target that is bound.

- Viewpoint puts back the state that the raw calls change: blending, the depth test and the depth mask, the colour mask,
  culling, the scissor and the line width.
- Leave unit 0 active, and leave no program and no vertex array of yours bound. Leave the target bound. If a callback
  changes one of these, Viewpoint puts it back and suspends the addon. The card says what was wrong.
- A callback that throws is suspended too.

## Cost

Viewpoint measures the time of each callback on the render thread and on the graphics card. See
[Measuring your addon](https://docs.projectviewpoint.org/performance/measuring-your-addon.md).

## The Gpu object

`DrawContext.gpu()` gives the `Gpu` of your addon. Use it to make programs, buffers, textures and meshes, and to draw
with them. Use it only in a draw callback. Outside a callback, each method throws an `IllegalStateException`.

- Make each object one time, and keep it. Use it again in each frame.
- Tell Viewpoint how much video memory your buffers and textures need, in `draw.gpuMiB` (64 MiB if you do not). Viewpoint
  gives that amount to the addon when it starts. A buffer or a texture past it makes the method throw. More than 128 MiB
  needs the permission `vram`, which the player must accept.
- Viewpoint sets no other limit: the graphics card of the player is the limit. The amount and the permission show the
  player what your addon uses. The card shows the amount and what the addon holds.
- Viewpoint frees all the objects of the addon when the addon goes off. You can close an object before that.

| Method | What it makes |
| --- | --- |
| `program(vertex, fragment)` | A program from the text of its two stages. Each text starts with its `#version` line. The same text gives the same program, compiled one time. An addon has 32 programs at most. |
| `buffer(bytes)` | A buffer of vertex data. Write to it with `upload(float[])`, `upload(int[])`, `upload(FloatBuffer)` or `upload(ByteBuffer)`. |
| `texture(width, height)` | A clear texture, 8 bits a channel with alpha. Write to it with `upload(int[])`, each pixel `0xAARRGGBB`. |
| `texture(picture)` | A texture of a PNG that `ctx.render().picture(bytes)` read on the main thread. |
| `mesh(buffer, 3, 2)` | The buffer read as vertices: each number gives the size of one attribute (`layout(location = 0)`, then 1), from 1 to 4 floats, 8 attributes at most. |
| `draw(program, mesh, primitive, first, count)` | Draws vertices of a mesh into the target that is bound. |
| `fullscreen(program)` | Draws one triangle that covers the target. The vertex stage makes its corners from `gl_VertexID`. |

A program keeps its values until you set them again:

- `set(name, numbers...)` for a `float` to a `vec4`, `setInt(name, value)`, `setMatrix(name, sixteen)`.
- `texture(sampler, slot, texture)` samples one of your textures, `input(sampler, slot, input)` one of the frame's:
  `DEPTH`, `NORMAL` or `ALBEDO`. A program samples two textures at most, at slots 0 and 1.
- A name that is not in the text of the program makes the method throw.
- The first row of a picture is at the texture coordinate `t = 0`.

Read the text of the program and the picture from your `data` folder. `read` gives the bytes later, on the main thread.
Give them to the callback, and make the objects in the callback:

```java title="BadgePart.java"
DataAssets data = ctx.assets().data();

data.read("badge.vert").then(vertex -> data.read("badge.frag").then(fragment -> data.read("badge.png").then(png -> {
    String vertexText = new String(vertex, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    String fragmentText = new String(fragment, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    Picture badge = ctx.render().picture(png);

    ctx.render().draw(DrawPoint.FINAL, context -> {
        Gpu gpu = context.gpu();

        if (program == null) {
            program = gpu.program(vertexText, fragmentText);
            mesh = gpu.mesh(gpu.buffer(QUAD.length * Float.BYTES).upload(QUAD), 2, 2); // place, then texture coordinate
            texture = gpu.texture(badge);
        }

        program.set("uRect", 0.8f, 0.8f, 0.95f, 0.95f).texture("uBadge", 0, texture);
        gpu.draw(program, mesh, Primitive.TRIANGLE_STRIP, 0, mesh.vertices());
    });
})));
```

`Gpu.draw` and `Gpu.fullscreen` put back the program and the vertex array that were bound before the callback.

## No memory addresses

An addon may not call LWJGL with a memory address. `org.lwjgl.system` (`MemoryUtil`, `MemoryStack`), `PointerBuffer`,
the `n`-prefixed functions and any call that takes a pointer make Viewpoint refuse the jar, and the card names the call.
Make your buffers with `BufferUtils`, and use the `Gpu` object instead.
